## Summary

There is no update mechanism of any kind: `autoUpdate` / `checkForUpdate` appear nowhere in the codebase. A user who installed a binary months ago has no way to learn that a newer release exists, short of visiting the repository. Comparable workbenches ship auto-updating desktop builds; we do not even notify.

## Current state

- **Version is visible, staleness is not.** `ScienceDiscovery version` prints the release version plus bundled Node/CPython/micromamba versions. Nothing ever compares that against what has since been published.
- **Releases already carry the right metadata.** `scripts/package-binary-release.sh` emits `VERSION` and `SHA256SUMS` next to the artifacts, and the binary-release flow already verifies downloads by pinned SHA-256 (that is how Node, CPython, micromamba, and the uv wheel are fetched). The building blocks for a verifiable update check exist.
- **Side-by-side versions already work.** The payload cache is digest-keyed (`~/.cache/science-discovery/payload/<payload-id>`) and "an upgrade does not overwrite an older extraction", so an older release stays runnable — rollback is feasible today.
- **Remote runners can silently drift.** The Runner SEA is versioned by the build's Git commit prefix, and a mismatch between the local control plane and an already-deployed remote runner only produces a warning; it does not block or redeploy. So a long-lived SSH target can keep running a months-old runner.
- **No documented upgrade contract.** There is no guide covering data-directory compatibility across releases, what a new binary rebuilds on first `serve`, or how to roll back (also noted in [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25)).

## Proposal

### 1. Update check (the part that matters most)

An opt-in check against a published release manifest — the existing `VERSION` + `SHA256SUMS` pair is already close to one.

- **Off by default in air-gapped installs**, and settable in system configuration. No telemetry beyond fetching the manifest; do not send an install identifier.
- Route the request through the configured network proxy, since proxy settings already exist.
- Surface the result quietly: a dismissible banner in the UI, a line in `ScienceDiscovery version`, and an explicit `--check-updates` for scripts.
- Fail silent on a network error. An offline workstation must never see an error toast because an update check could not reach the internet.

### 2. Self-update (optional second step)

`ScienceDiscovery update` that downloads the new artifact, verifies it against `SHA256SUMS` (ideally a signature too), swaps it atomically, and keeps the previous binary so a rollback is one command. The digest-keyed payload cache means the old version's extracted runtime is still there.

For Docker and source mode, print the right command instead of attempting anything — `docker compose pull` / `git pull && ./scripts/start-stack.sh` — rather than pretending a binary self-update applies.

### 3. Upgrade contract

Document, and enforce in code:

- what the data directory guarantees across versions, and what the first `serve` after an upgrade rebuilds;
- refusing to open a data directory written by a newer release, rather than half-migrating it;
- redeploying the matching Runner SEA to remote hosts when the control plane updates, instead of only warning about the mismatch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user on an outdated release is told so, in the UI and on the CLI.
- [ ] The check is opt-in/opt-out, proxy-aware, and silent on failure.
- [ ] No update path installs an artifact whose SHA-256 was not verified.
- [ ] Rollback to the previous version is documented and works.
- [ ] Docker and source-mode users get correct upgrade instructions rather than a binary self-update.
- [ ] Remote runner drift is resolved automatically or reported as an actionable error.

## Open questions

- Where would the release manifest live, given the canonical repository is on GitCode and GitHub is a mirror? It needs one stable URL.
- Should releases be signed, or is SHA-256 against a manifest over HTTPS sufficient for this threat model?
- Default for the update check on a fresh install: on or off?
oldest.title: [Feature]: Notify users of new releases, and support self-update

## Problem

In the `feat/jiuwenswarm` remote Shell Execution flow, the API polls the Runner after the Runner accepts a job. If a status request throws because of a transient communication error, the current implementation can finalize the local record as `unknown / unconfirmed`. This means the remote result has not been confirmed; it does **not** prove that the remote job failed or that the full Agent/skill workflow passed.

## Trigger confirmed from the code

- In `services/api/src/shell-executions.ts`, a `getShellExecution` exception reaches the outer error handler and calls `finish`, turning an accepted execution into `unknown / unconfirmed`. A transient observation error is not sufficiently separated from an authoritative remote terminal state.
- Once the local record is terminal, the normal `execution_status` path does not reconcile that record with the Runner using the original Execution ID. Executions left behind by API restarts or Runner reconnections also need an explicit reconciliation policy.
- The underlying reason for an SSH/Runner status request error still needs investigation. Without a correlated error cause and channel logs, `fetch failed` alone does not establish whether the NPU job, SSH connection, or server failed.

## Suggested reproduction

1. Submit a long-running Shell Execution to a remote Runner and confirm that the Runner accepted it.
2. Make only one **status request** fail transiently while keeping the remote job running.
3. Verify that the API keeps polling the **same Execution ID**, obtains the Runner's authoritative result after connectivity returns, and does not resubmit the command.
4. Also cover consecutive failures, API restart, Runner reconnection, and the complete Agent → skill → NPU artifact flow. See the related end-to-end test in #168.

## Expected fix and acceptance criteria

- Retry recoverable observation errors within a bound, resetting the consecutive-failure count after a successful query. If the result remains unavailable after the threshold, preserve the uncertainty explicitly instead of reporting success or a job failure.
- Provide safe Runner-authoritative reconciliation for `unknown` and restart-orphaned executions without replaying the command.
- Log a correlatable Execution ID, underlying error cause/code, consecutive-failure count, and Runner connection state so an observation-path failure can be distinguished from an actual job failure.
- Cover fault injection in CI without an NPU, and validate the final artifacts through the full Agent/skill workflow in an NPU-enabled environment.

recent.author: wyhohyw
recent.body:
## Description

When the Nightly workflow runs UT and ST with the `daily` profile, both test jobs produce raw coverage data, but the Coverage job does not receive the corresponding artifacts. As a result, coverage merging fails and the coverage summary is not updated.

Affected run:

- Nightly run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/35919083156
- Commit: `9c5a5097336ab5342050dc07f9b14c3ccfce9cd0`
- Actual UT output: `.ci-results/daily-ut/tagged/coverage`
- Actual ST output: `.ci-results/daily-st/tagged/coverage`

The UT and ST jobs themselves completed successfully and wrote coverage data. The failure occurs while handing that data off to the Coverage job.

## Root cause

`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs` includes the profile name in the output label for profiles other than `pr`:

```js
const label = dimensions.length
  ? 'query'
  : profileName === 'pr'
    ? slice
    : `${profileName}-${slice}`;
```

This produces the following paths:

- `pr + ut` → `.ci-results/ut/tagged/coverage`
- `daily + ut` → `.ci-results/daily-ut/tagged/coverage`
- `daily + st` → `.ci-results/daily-st/tagged/coverage`

However, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` still uses profile-independent upload paths:

```yaml
path: .ci-results/ut/tagged/coverage
```

and:

```yaml
path: .ci-results/st/tagged/coverage
```

When Nightly selects the `daily` profile, neither hard-coded path exists. `actions/upload-artifact` therefore reports that no files were found and does not create the `ut-coverage` or `st-coverage` artifact. The Coverage job cannot download those artifacts, merges zero Node.js and Python files, and fails.

This is not a dashboard input-path issue. The data is never uploaded as a workflow artifact, and a later job cannot access the previous job's local workspace directly.

## Regression timeline

- PR #148 introduced the `daily` profile and the `daily-ut` / `daily-st` output naming:
  https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/148
- PR #150 changed Coverage to reuse data produced by the UT/ST jobs, but used hard-coded `ut` / `st` upload paths that do not account for non-`pr` profiles:
  https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/150
- PR #158 enabled hidden-file uploads for the result artifacts, but did not update the coverage artifact paths:
  https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/158

The previous successful Nightly run was:

- https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/35782010015

That run started before PR #150 was merged, so it did not use the current UT/ST coverage-artifact handoff. The `daily-ut` naming introduced by PR #148 is intentional; the regression is the profile-independent artifact path added by PR #150.

## Suggested fix

Avoid hard-coding the `ut` and `st` result directories in the workflow. Possible approaches include:

1. Compute the actual result directory from `${{ inputs.profile || 'pr' }}` and upload coverage from that directory.
2. Have the test runner expose the resolved coverage path as an explicit step output.
3. Use a constrained glob that covers `ut`, `daily-ut`, `st`, and `daily-st` without mixing data from unrelated profiles or slices.

An explicitly computed path is preferable because it avoids accidentally merging data from multiple profiles.

## Acceptance criteria

- The `pr` profile continues to upload and merge UT/ST coverage.
- Nightly with the `daily` profile uploads coverage from `daily-ut` and `daily-st`.
- The Coverage job downloads `ut-coverage` and `st-coverage` and generates non-empty Node.js and Python summaries.
- If UT or ST produces no coverage, the summary identifies the missing layer instead of reporting a misleading zero-file merge.
- The Release workflow continues to skip coverage generation and upload.

recent.author: zy95-12
recent.body:
## Motivation

A recent real E2E literature-review run (DRB-59) exposed a reliability gap in the literature-research handoff. The main agent launched six literature-search subagents. Four delivered source artifacts; two spent many tool calls finding sources but failed while attempting to write large Markdown source packages in a single `run_shell` call. Both failed model responses hit the 16,384-output-token limit, their tool arguments were truncated, and no usable artifact was handed back from those two tasks. The parent retried them with smaller writes, but the overall run reached its 60-minute limit before a final report was produced.

The observed failure is in *packaging and handing off the research*, not evidence that the searches themselves were uniformly bad. The current `skills/literature-searcher/SKILL.md` already describes a deduplicated JSON source package, but it does not tell an agent how to checkpoint a long search, bound each write, or resume from partial results. In this run, the delegated instructions instead asked for long Markdown packages with verbatim abstracts, which increased the size of one-shot tool calls.

## Proposed direction for discussion

1. **Make source packages incremental and durable.** Write a small, validated batch of records after each search phase or connector result, then update a compact manifest with counts, query coverage, gaps, and completion status. Keep the downstream JSON contract, or define an explicitly compatible JSONL/manifest handoff. Avoid asking the model to emit an entire large artifact as one shell argument. Preserve DOI/URL, database, citation, and abstract availability without inventing missing metadata.
2. **Keep research content out of the active conversation once saved.** Pass artifact paths plus a concise source index/coverage summary to the parent. Use context compression/checkpoints for long-running research when available, while preserving provenance and the next action. Compression can reduce input-history pressure; it cannot raise the per-response output-token limit that caused these two failures.
3. **Recover cleanly from interrupted writes.** Detect truncated or invalid tool arguments before dispatch, keep already written records, and retry only the unfinished batch at a smaller size. Surface the failure and checkpoint location in the child trajectory so the parent can resume without repeating all searches.
4. **Leave time for synthesis.** The parent should be able to use completed, validated source packages and explicitly report remaining coverage gaps if a retry cannot finish within the run budget. A full retry should not consume the entire report-writing window.

## Questions to settle

- Should the canonical handoff remain one `literature_sources.json`, or should agents append JSONL records and materialize/validate the JSON at the end?
- What is the smallest useful checkpoint (per query, per connector response, or fixed-size record batch), and who owns deduplication across checkpoints?
- Which fields must survive context compression for a parent or replacement subagent to continue the search without losing citation provenance?
- Should the runtime's truncated-tool-argument recovery be tracked here as a dependency or in a separate generic issue?

## Acceptance criteria

- A literature-searcher task with a source package larger than one model response writes valid, deduplicated records progressively and returns a usable handoff without a giant one-shot tool call.
- If a write or model response is interrupted, a retry resumes from the last valid checkpoint and does not duplicate or silently drop sources.
- The parent can consume completed packages, identify missing coverage, and produce a clearly qualified partial report before its deadline.
- An automated test injects an interrupted/truncated write; DRB-59 can serve as a real E2E follow-up, with its report quality assessed separately from this deterministic recovery test.

Related: #141 discusses the two subagent orchestration paths. This issue focuses on the literature-research workflow and artifact handoff, which matter on either path.

recent.body:
### 🚀 Background Description ScienceDiscovery's backend is currently the TypeScript `services/api` (port 4310, `http/index.ts` at about 3,500 lines, `store.ts` at about 5,600 lines, depending on about 50k lines of `packages/*`, with the agent loop also running in Node). The frontend `apps/web` talks to it through about 260 HTTP endpoints plus SSE. [JiuwenSwarm](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm) already provides general agent capabilities: multi-agent team/Swarm, skills and skill self-evolution, permission approval, sessions and projects, MCP, scheduled tasks, and the jiuwenbox sandbox. This issue proposes: **keep the existing TypeScript frontend, reuse JiuwenSwarm as the main Agent backend as much as possible, and keep the science-specific modules (evolve, idea-tree, memory-graph, artifact/provenance, etc.) as standalone backends.** E2E cases serve as the acceptance spec for the migration. ### Goals and plan **Short term (Sep 30):** 10 E2E cases pass with no quality regression, and the corresponding 10 scenarios are usable; release a minor-version RC. **October:** Refine step by step, complete the migration, and make all E2E cases usable. **Long term:** Gradually switch to the componentized version of JiuwenSwarm (the `AgentRuntime` public API) and evolve in sync with JiuwenSwarm; gate on contract tests, switching the chat core first and the remaining domains afterward. The 10 E2E cases will be decided by Zhang Yi by Sep 21. **Baseline version:** Fixed on JiuwenSwarm 0.2.6. The interface and event analysis in this issue was read from the local `0.2.5.beta1` code and needs to be rechecked against 0.2.6. ### Overall migration philosophy 1. **Reuse JiuwenSwarm first and do not modify it by default; intrusive modification is allowed when necessary.** Use its chat, sessions, team/Swarm, permissions, skills, MCP, and scheduled tasks directly. Intrusive modifications are applied as patches on the fixed version (0.2.6) and merged back upstream later. 2. **Keep the frontend contract unchanged and translate in one place only.** The frontend speaks HTTP + SSE (32 event types); JiuwenSwarm speaks WebSocket (`req / res / event`, about 400 methods). A new **adapter** does the translation, with essentially no frontend changes; the goal is to eliminate endpoints that need a wrapper to adapt. 3. **Scientific value stays in standalone backends.** artifact, provenance, review, evolve, idea-tree, memory-graph, and runner each have their own process, data directory, and token; the frontend reaches them through the adapter's reverse proxy, and the agent calls them through MCP tools. 4. **Each piece of state has exactly one owner.** Sessions and projects belong to JiuwenSwarm, science metadata belongs to each standalone service, and the adapter only handles what nobody else owns (run event log, settings and secrets, permission audit, usage statistics). 5. **Tests are the spec, and the agent implements by "red-to-green".** First turn the existing E2E and contract tests into an acceptance baseline that can target any backend, then implement feature domains one by one; behavior without a covering case does not count as migrated. 6. **Switching can be done in batches.** For routes not yet migrated, the adapter can fall back to the old `services/api` and switch traffic domain by domain (this requires both sides to share session IDs, see Open decisions). ### Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR UI["Web UI (apps/web, TypeScript, essentially unchanged)"] subgraph ADP["Adapter (newly written, Python)"] direction TB A1["HTTP + SSE routes (about 260)"] A2["Bearer auth, users mapped to user_id"] A3["run registry and event log (seq, resume)"] A4["Event mapping (32 frontend event types)"] A5["Storage for settings, secrets, permission audit, usage statistics"] end subgraph JW["JiuwenSwarm (reused, not forked)"] direction TB GW["Gateway /ws"] AS["AgentServer"] CAP["Sessions and projects / Team and Swarm / Permission rails
Skill and evolution / MCP client / Cron / jiuwenbox"] GW --> AS --> CAP end subgraph SVC["Standalone backends (own process, data directory, token)"] direction TB S1["artifact / provenance / CAS
extracted from services/api"] S2["evolve
Python already exists, TS orchestration layer moved in"] S3["idea-tree
split out of evolve"] S4["memory-graph
already a standalone service"] S5["paper parsing"] S6["runner + compute
environments, execution, remote hosts, NPU"] S7["science MCP services
biomedicine / UniProt / llm-wiki"] end UI -->|"HTTP + SSE"| ADP ADP -->|"WebSocket req / res / event"| GW ADP -->|"reverse proxy"| SVC CAP -->|"MCP tools"| SVC ADP -.->|"Fallback for unmigrated routes (optional)"| LEGACY["old services/api"] ``` In the short term the adapter connects to the Gateway's WebSocket (broadest coverage); in the long term it switches to the `AgentRuntime` componentized interface.
The two ways to connect the adapter, and a few facts about JiuwenSwarm's connection layer **The two ways to connect the adapter:** | | A. Connect to the Gateway's WebSocket (recommended for the first version) | B. Embed `AgentRuntime` in-process | |---|---|---| | Coverage | All about 400 methods, including team/swarm, skills, mcp, config | Only covers single-agent sessions, chat, permissions, and model and mode catalogs; the Process CLI docs explicitly do not accept Team / Workflow / AutoHarness root modes | | Types | Handwritten, no schema | Python dataclasses, typed | | Stability | Protocol is ready-made, validated by the React frontend and the TUI | Public API was only just completed (`f29c060c`, `8773691e`), stability unknown | **A few facts about JiuwenSwarm's connection layer (which the adapter must fill in itself):** - Identity comes from connection parameters (`user_id`, `session_id`, `mode`, `agent_id`, `app_id`) or request headers, and no token validation was found, so the frontend's existing Bearer auth must be done by the adapter. - `seq` and `stream_id` on event frames are optional fields, and no mechanism was found for replaying by sequence number after a disconnect, so the frontend's `runs/:id/events?after=N` resume relies on the adapter storing its own event log. - The payloads of `chat.delta / final / reasoning` are flat `{session_id, content}`; `chat.tool_call / tool_update / tool_result / ask_user_question / subtask_update / subagent_activity / usage_*` and similar keep their full payloads.
### Migration approach per module | Scope | Migration approach | |---|---| | Chat, sessions, projects, permissions, models, MCP, skills | **Reuse JiuwenSwarm + adapter mapping** (59 approximate mappings, 21 direct mappings) | | Runs and event log, settings and secrets, permission audit, skill library versions, usage statistics | **Adapter-built** (JiuwenSwarm has none, 66 items) | | Science toolset (run_shell, execute Python, web, artifact, etc.) | **Provided again as MCP** to JiuwenSwarm's agent (a new major item) | | artifact / provenance / CAS, review | **Standalone service**: reuse the existing TS packages plus a thin HTTP layer, no rewrite | | evolve, idea-tree, memory-graph, paper | **Standalone service**: the evolve orchestration layer moves into Python, idea-tree is split out of evolve, memory-graph is almost as is, paper gets a wrapper layer | | runner, environments, remote hosts, NPU | **Keep runner + pass through**; remote host and NPU logic moves out with runner, in the second batch | | Scheduled tasks, science gateway MCP | **Reuse directly** JiuwenSwarm's `schedule.*` and MCP config | | Frontend | Essentially unchanged; hide unsupported entry points and clean up dead code |
Full module migration table (current state → target → approach) Legend: **Reuse** = use JiuwenSwarm directly; **Adapt** = the adapter does the mapping; **Build ourselves** = JiuwenSwarm does not have it; **Standalone** = standalone backend; **Keep as is** = essentially untouched. | Module | Current state | Target | Migration approach | |---|---|---|---| | Chat and agent loop | `native-agent`: 128-round loop, parallel tools, loop-guard, deferred `tool_search` | JiuwenSwarm's agent loop | **Reuse + adapt**: `chat.send / interrupt / user_answer`; the adapter adds a run registry, event log, and SSE resume, and synthesizes events such as `run.queued / started` that upstream does not have | | Context assembly and compaction | `packages/context` (about 3.5k lines) | JiuwenSwarm's context compaction | **Reuse**, our own assembly is not migrated | | Sessions and projects | JSON blob in `catalog_state` | JiuwenSwarm's session and project storage | **Adapt**: `session.*`, `project.*`; `SessionDetail` is assembled by the adapter; deletion cascades to clean up runner kernel and memory-graph | | Permissions and approval | `governance`, epoch, `permission_authorizations` | JiuwenSwarm's approval rails | **Adapt**: approval maps to `chat.ask_user_question` + `chat.user_answer`, `permissions.*`; **build ourselves** the epoch and audit table | | Models, providers | `model`, models.dev catalog, AES-GCM keys | JiuwenSwarm config | **Adapt**: `models.*`, `config.*`; quota, timeout, and proxy go in adapter storage | | MCP | Custom servers, OAuth, Inspector | JiuwenSwarm's MCP | **Reuse + adapt**: `mcp.*`; Inspector needs the adapter to bring its own MCP client, whether OAuth is covered needs a spike | | Skill and review drafts | `skill`, review drafts | JiuwenSwarm's skills and evolution | **Reuse + adapt**: `skills.*`, `evolution.*` | | Skill library versioning | commit / 409 conflict / dryRun / rollback / diff / proposals (14 endpoints) | adapter | **Build ourselves**: JiuwenSwarm only has `versions.list` | | Sub-agents, specialists, plans | `task` tool, `specialist` (8 built in), `update_plan` | JiuwenSwarm's team, agent_templates, todo | **Adapt**: built-in specialists become agent templates; `todo.updated` corresponds to `plan.updated`; the reviewer checkpoint has no counterpart, degraded | | Settings, secrets, proxy, quota | About 18 settings endpoints, several encrypted credential tables | adapter storage | **Build ourselves** | | Files, workspace, trajectory | `workspace` (about 5.2k lines) | `files.*`, `container_file_http`, `trajectory_http` | **Adapt**: upload conflict policy and workspace binding are built by the adapter | | Usage and quota page | `UsagePage` | Session usage mapping, cross-session statistics built ourselves | **Adapt + build ourselves** | | Scheduled tasks | `scheduler` (43 lines), `agent_timers` | JiuwenSwarm's `schedule.*` / `cron.*` | **Reuse**; semantics of agent-set timers to be confirmed | | Science toolset | `packages/tools` (about 2.7k lines): `run_shell`, execute Python, web search/fetch, `task`, `update_plan`, etc. | Provided as MCP to JiuwenSwarm's agent | **New major item**: today's tools are all written in the Node loop, so a new set must be provided; the tool list needs to be inventoried one by one | | artifact / provenance / CAS | `artifact-manager`, `provenance`, `cas`, `trajectory`, etc., about 12k lines of TS, with the logic inside `services/api` | Standalone service | **Standalone**: extract into a thin HTTP service reusing the existing TS packages, no rewrite; about 40 frontend endpoints; artifact ingestion is triggered by tool results or workspace file changes | | artifact review, claims, evidence | `reviewer-specialist` | artifact service + JiuwenSwarm sub-agent | **Standalone**, the review agent is carried by a sub-agent | | evolve | About 11k lines of Python + about 4.3k lines of TS orchestration layer (`services/api/src/evolution/`) | Standalone evolve service | **Standalone**: **recommended** to move the orchestration layer into Python with its own storage; the LLM callback proxy (`/internal/evolve-llm/…`) is provided by the adapter using JiuwenSwarm's model config; does not overlap with JiuwenSwarm's RSI / auto-harness (the former evolves candidate science programs, the latter evolves skills and harnesses). Alternative: first extract the TS orchestration layer into a small standalone process, at the cost of keeping two tech stacks long term | | idea-tree | TS package (about 1.6k lines) + Python router inside evolve + `python-client.ts` | Standalone idea-tree service | **Standalone**: split two routers out of evolve, own state directory; Event mapping (32 frontend event types) | Frontend event | Source | |---|---| | `assistant.delta`, `assistant.thinking.delta` | Direct: `chat.delta`, `chat.reasoning` | | `tool.started / output / completed` | Converted: `chat.tool_call / tool_update / tool_result` | | `run.completed / failed / cancelled` | Converted: `chat.final`, `chat.error`, `chat.interrupt_result` | | `permission.required` | Converted: `chat.ask_user_question` / `plan.approval_required`; the answer must carry back `interaction_id`, `source` | | `plan.updated`, `subagent.*`, `session.updated`, `run.status`, `agent.phase` | Converted: `todo.updated`, `chat.subtask_update`, `chat.subagent_activity`, `session.lifecycle.updated`, `chat.processing_status` | | `run.queued / started / history.truncated`, `assistant.snapshot`, `assistant.response.started`, `permission.resolved` | Synthesized by the adapter (upstream has no run concept) | | `workspace.changed`, `artifact.upserted`, `artifact_review.completed`, `idea_tree.phase`, `idea_research.created`, `evolve_run.created`, `remote_job.proposed`, `agent.record` and the `evidence` field | Triggered by standalone backends or tool results; the adapter merges them into the same event stream | The mapping above is inferred from event names and payload whitelists; exact fields must be calibrated against real traffic captured in the spike.
### Sub-tasks and dependencies Split into 21 sub-tasks by inter-interface dependencies; each sub-task has that domain's interface list, non-interface tasks, dependencies, items to be confirmed, and acceptance. "Batch" is the earliest startable level computed from the dependencies: sub-tasks in the same batch do not depend on each other and can run in parallel. - The number of interfaces that "need wrapper" = approximate mapping + adapter-implemented, i.e. the part to be assessed for the goal "eliminate interfaces that need a wrapper adapter", 125 in total. **Task list** (GitHub tracks the completion progress of each sub-task): Batch 0: - [x] #86 Acceptance baseline and protocol calibration (spike) (Prerequisites: none, no interface list) Batch 1: - [x] #87 Adapter core: auth, connection pool, run and event log, storage and proxy framework (Prerequisites: #86, 1 interface, 1 needs wrapper) Batch 2: - [x] #88 Sessions and projects (Prerequisites: #87, 13 interfaces, 7 need wrapper) - [x] #91 Models, providers and global settings (Prerequisites: #87, 27 interfaces, 26 need wrapper) - [ ] #93 Skills and skill libraries (Prerequisites: #87, 36 interfaces, 30 need wrapper) Batch 3: - [x] #89 Chat and runs (Prerequisites: #87, #88, 10 interfaces, 5 need wrapper) - [ ] #94 Files, workspace, trajectory (Prerequisites: #88, 7 interfaces, 7 need wrapper) - [ ] #96 runner, environments and execution pass-through (Prerequisites: #87, #91, 28 interfaces, 1 needs wrapper) Batch 4: - [x] #90 Permissions and approvals (Prerequisites: #88, #89, 8 interfaces, 7 need wrapper) - [x] #92 MCP and data sources (Prerequisites: #87, #89, #91, 21 interfaces, 17 need wrapper) - [x] #95 Planning and sub-agents (Prerequisites: #89, 8 interfaces, 7 need wrapper) - [ ] #100 memory-graph integration (Prerequisites: #87, #88, #89, 14 interfaces, 0 need wrapper) - [x] #103 Usage (Prerequisites: #89, #91, 5 interfaces, 5 need wrapper) - [ ] #104 Remote hosts and NPU (compute) (Prerequisites: #96, 17 interfaces, 0 need wrapper) - [ ] #105 Plugins (Prerequisites: #88, #94, 6 interfaces, 6 need wrapper) Batch 5: - [x] #97 Science toolset MCP-ification (Prerequisites: #92, #96, no interface list) Batch 6: - [ ] #98 artifact / provenance / CAS service (including papers) (Prerequisites: #87, #94, #97, 32 interfaces, 0 need wrapper) Batch 7: - [ ] #99 artifact review, claims and evidence (Prerequisites: #95, #98, 12 interfaces, 4 need wrapper) - [ ] #101 idea-tree service (Prerequisites: #87, #93, #97, #98, 6 interfaces, 0 need wrapper) - [ ] #106 Cross-domain wrap-up: workbench search, dead code cleanup, packaging and startup (Prerequisites: #88, #98, #100, 3 interfaces, 1 needs wrapper) Batch 8: - [ ] #102 evolve service (Prerequisites: #87, #91, #96, #98, #101, 5 interfaces, 1 needs wrapper)
Dependency graph ```mermaid flowchart LR n86["#86 Acceptance baseline and protocol calibration"] n87["#87 Adapter core"] n88["#88 Sessions and projects"] n89["#89 Chat and runs"] n90["#90 Permissions and approvals"] n91["#91 Models, providers and settings"] n92["#92 MCP and data sources"] n93["#93 Skills and skill libraries"] n94["#94 Files, workspace, trajectory"] n95["#95 Planning and sub-agents"] n96["#96 runner and environments"] n97["#97 Science toolset MCP-ification"] n98["#98 artifact / provenance"] n99["#99 Review, claims and evidence"] n100["#100 memory-graph"] n101["#101 idea-tree"] n102["#102 evolve"] n103["#103 Usage"] n104["#104 Remote hosts and NPU"] n105["#105 Plugins"] n106["#106 Cross-domain wrap-up"] n86 --> n87 n87 --> n88 n87 --> n89 n88 --> n89 n88 --> n90 n89 --> n90 n87 --> n91 n87 --> n92 n89 --> n92 n91 --> n92 n87 --> n93 n88 --> n94 n89 --> n95 n87 --> n96 n91 --> n96 n92 --> n97 n96 --> n97 n87 --> n98 n94 --> n98 n97 --> n98 n95 --> n99 n98 --> n99 n87 --> n100 n88 --> n100 n89 --> n100 n87 --> n101 n93 --> n101 n97 --> n101 n98 --> n101 n87 --> n102 n91 --> n102 n96 --> n102 n98 --> n102 n101 --> n102 n89 --> n103 n91 --> n103 n96 --> n104 n88 --> n105 n94 --> n105 n88 --> n106 n98 --> n106 n100 --> n106 ```
### Test strategy: guarantee features with E2E cases **Tests are the spec.** The agent writes the implementation; the cases decide whether it is correct. The existing `test/` has 44 specs (27 journeys, about 79 cases, approximate), the `.e2e` Playwright isolated stack, the scripted stub LLM endpoint and the `.ci/test-catalog.mjs` tag system, all reusable; but coverage of the 259 interface rows is far from enough, so fill it in before starting. | Layer | Content | |---|---| | L1 contract diff | Record each interface's request and response on the old backend with the stub LLM as the baseline; the new backend replays and diffs; every interface row must have a case or be marked "no migration needed" | | L2 event golden trace | Scripted scenarios (tool call, approval, interrupt, sub-agent, error, reconnect and resume) record the old backend's SSE; the new backend is compared event by event across the 32 event types | | L3 Playwright E2E | The existing 27 journeys are first pointed at the new stack as is; then add about 25–40 new science-feature cases | | L4 behavior acceptance | A few representative science tasks run once on each of the old and new backends, compared manually | Baselines and assertions are read-only to the agent; changing a baseline to "go green" must be reviewed by a human; security negative cases are reviewed by a human.
L3 new case scope and admission criteria **L3 new case scope:** artifact versions and provenance, artifact review, claims and evidence chips, one full evolve run and stop, idea-tree research flow, memory-graph write and cleanup, environment creation and installation, sandbox network allowlist, skill library commit and rollback, cascading cleanup when deleting a session or project, reconnecting to the same run after a disconnect, no execution after permission is denied. **Admission and completion criteria:** - [ ] A feature domain counts as migrated when all its L1 rows, related L2 scenarios and related L3 journeys are green; - [ ] Security-related negative cases are required: auth failure and privilege escalation, approval denied, sandbox escape, access outside the network allowlist, old authorization invalidated after epoch rotation; these cases themselves must be reviewed by a human; - [ ] Baseline files and assertions are read-only to the agent; any change that modifies a baseline to "go green" must be reviewed by a human, to prevent the agent from changing cases just to pass them; - [ ] Cases are registered in `.ci/test-catalog.mjs` and tagged `layer:e2e`, `llm:stub` and so on, plugged into the existing CI layers; - [ ] The new backend can be started with one command in the `.e2e` isolated stack; formal E2E must not use the manual-trial port 4310 or its fixed data directory; - [ ] Output a coverage gap report every week: interface rows not covered by cases, event types not covered by golden traces.
### Open decisions 1. **Who fixes JiuwenSwarm bugs and who is the patch owner** (see risk 3). 2. **Sandbox**: keep using the runner's own bwrap / Seatbelt, or switch to jiuwenbox. 3. **Staged cutover**: whether the adapter falls back to the old `services/api` for unmigrated routes (requires both sides to share session IDs).
Public interfaces involved, and relationship to other modules **Public interfaces involved** - **Frontend contract (unchanged)**: the `/api/*` HTTP interfaces, the SSE events of `RunStreamEvent` (`packages/schema/src/session.ts`), Bearer auth, and the dev-environment Vite proxy for `/api` and `/health` (`127.0.0.1:4310`). - **New**: the adapter's WebSocket calls to the JiuwenSwarm Gateway (depending on the `ReqMethod` / `EventType` enums); the MCP tools each standalone backend exposes to the agent. - **Existing external interfaces of each standalone backend** (which the adapter must connect to): runner's 39 route groups, evolve's 7 (`/runs` returns NDJSON, `/idea-tree/*`), memory-graph's 27. - **Callback direction**: the evolve sandbox calls `/internal/evolve-llm/:runId/v1/chat/completions` (run-level token, not user auth), which the adapter provides after migration. **Relationship to other modules** - `services/api`: gradually replaced by the adapter; during migration it can serve as the fallback target for unmigrated routes. - `packages/*`: artifact-manager, cas, provenance, workspace, trajectory and so on are extracted and reused as the artifact service; `context`, `orchestration`, `plan`, `native-agent` and so on are replaced by JiuwenSwarm together with the agent loop. `packages/schema` (about 8.4k lines) is the contract hub shared by frontend and backend, and must be taken along or the contract generated when extracting services. - `scripts/check-architecture.mjs`: the boundary rules between packages (packages must not import `services/` or `apps/`, etc.) remain useful when splitting; the new adapter and services must follow them. - CI: contract tests and E2E need reworking; the externally facing contract part of `services/api/src/server.test.ts` (about 7500 lines) can be turned into contract tests for the adapter.
Limitations of this analysis and references **Limitations of this analysis:** - The route list comes from reading `services/api/src/http/index.ts` and the route files under `http/`, plus the route files of runner, evolve and memory-graph; "not called by the frontend" comes from a grep over `apps/web/src`. - On the JiuwenSwarm side, only the message model, WebSocket handshake and dispatch, event payload construction and the public types of `runtime/` were read; for the other methods only the names were seen. The parameter keys of `chat.send`, the payload keys of each response, and the behavior when multiple clients subscribe to the same session are **not verified**. - The following are marked "to be confirmed": the backend route for the frontend login handshake, stopping and resuming a single sub-agent, whether MCP deletion and OAuth are covered by JiuwenSwarm, and the semantics of agent-set timers. - The total number of features is 58 (35 core, 15 auxiliary, 8 experimental). `agent-runtime`, `direct-mode`, `plan-mode`, `execution-modes` and `science-sources` under `packages/` no longer have `src`, only stale build artifacts, and do not count as features. **References:** - JiuwenSwarm: https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm - JiuwenSwarm's E2A protocol and event enums: `docs/en/E2A-protocol.md`, `jiuwenswarm/common/schema/message.py` - JiuwenSwarm single-agent Runtime public API and one-shot execution entry: `jiuwenswarm/runtime/service.py`, `docs/en/Process_CLI_Machine.md`
### Risks | # | Risk | Description | Requirement | Decision point | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Impact of JiuwenSwarm version upgrades and componentization refactoring | After an upgrade or refactor, the methods and events the adapter depends on may change; JiuwenSwarm has recently been filling in the `runtime/` public API and one-shot execution entry (`f29c060c`, `8773691e`), and componentization is still evolving | Features are unaffected after upgrades, and stay in sync with JiuwenSwarm's evolution | Upgrade cadence (follow every release, or reserve one release for an adaptation iteration); when to start switching to the componentized version | | 2 | Whether JiuwenSwarm's internal errors reach the frontend in full | The known error channels are the `res` frame (`ok:false` + `error` + `code`), `chat.error`, `execution.error`, `runtime.error`, but whether the cause chain is complete, whether errors are swallowed, and whether retry info is included are not verified | Internal errors reach the frontend completely and understandably, and the run wraps up normally | Which error issues need intrusive modification (confirm after the spike) | | 3 | JiuwenSwarm's own bugs and intrusive modification: who fixes them and how they are merged back | Intrusive modification is not ruled out, but ownership is unclear when there are bugs, and patches may conflict with later upstream versions | Bugs have a clear owner and handling path; intrusive modifications can be merged back upstream without conflicting with later versions | Who fixes bugs; who the patch owner is | | 4 | Pace for Sep 30 and October | The 10 E2E cases for Sep 30 and the full migration in October are on a tight schedule | The 10 E2E cases work on Sep 30 with no degradation in quality; all E2E cases work in October | Scope and staffing needed (assess once the case list and spike results are out); what can be pushed back | | 5 | Agent behavior differences | The 128-turn cap, parallel tools, loop-guard and deferred `tool_search` may behave differently once replaced by JiuwenSwarm, which is the change users notice most easily | The same science task performs no worse on the new backend | Which representative tasks to use for acceptance; the criterion for "no worse" and who judges it |

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
Reorganize the Chinese and English core documentation around six research capabilities: scientific sandbox, Idea Tree, RSI for scientific artifacts, ScienceMemory/Reviewer, Specialists, and scientific MCP/Skills.

Replace implementation-heavy introductions with accessible feature articles that explain the research problem, how the capability helps, and what users can inspect or reuse. Keep existing core URLs, add three new capability pages per language, and reorder the documentation landing pages. Preserve the previous execution/workspace reference and Idea Tree implementation details in reference/ and developer-docs/, with navigation and contextual links.

Check claims against current code as well as design documents: distinguish Bubblewrap and Seatbelt, experimental proposals from executed experiments, artifact optimization from model training, and recorded evidence/review findings from scientific proof. Describe optional memory, session-enabled automatic report reviews, read-only Reviewer feedback, actual Specialist fields, and skill draft confirmation without promising unsupported automation.

Specialist and MCP/Skill articles lead with scientific use cases and enumerate the actual included capabilities: all 8 built-in Specialists, all 17 bundled Skills, and the scientific source integrations. Add bilingual advanced setup guides for custom Specialists and local/Git Skill import, including JiuwenSwarm-specific availability controls; reuse the existing MCP setup guide. Catalog names were cross-checked against code.

Validation: Markdown lint and local links passed across 118 documents; git diff whitespace checks passed; existing links to removed core headings were checked (none found). Documentation only; no runtime, benchmark prompt, assertion, or scoring changes, and no paid E2E run.

items.author: zy95-12
items.body:
The compression walkthrough assumed readers understood evolution terminology and did not explain how to interpret the reported score. Rewrite the Chinese and English tutorials as “使用PUCT优化一个文本压缩算法” / “Use PUCT to optimize a text compression algorithm” with eight sections: background, preparation, starting the task, requirements, optimization, results, caveats, and related documentation. Consolidate the two overlapping domain guides into evolve-a-solution.md in both languages, delete run-an-evolution-search.md, and update all incoming links and navigation titles.

The tutorial uses the retained real run (16 expansions, 4 workers; gate 0.5757 → 0.9540; held-out 0.9224) to explain the changes from Huffman to context-based range coding. It explicitly explains the generated evaluator’s normalization and clipping, so 0.9224 cannot be mistaken for 92.24% size reduction. It also documents observed checkpoint behavior and synthetic-corpus limitations.

Add a real PUCT-COMPRESS E2E that reads the tutorial prompt, chooses PUCT through the browser, acknowledges checkpoints when needed and waits for the background search. Completion requires a normally finished main/search run and readable persisted code matching the selected candidate. It accepts a seed that remained best and has no score/improvement/candidate-count threshold. Separately retain the final held-out score, baseline/best gate values and frozen evaluator; missing held-out scores remain unavailable with a note rather than becoming zero or being replaced by gate scores.

The case joins the existing daily real-E2E selection and stays outside mocked PR gates. A tagged UT covers score extraction, zero/no-improvement outcomes and unavailable scores. No existing case is disabled or reclassified.

Validation: project build, targeted E2E TypeScript check, 3 scorecard UTs, E2E metadata/catalog checks, real Playwright discovery, and Markdown lint and links across 100 documents passed. The new real E2E passed in 5m33s on an isolated Swarm stack (memory graph off, 24 GiB limit, two-hour budget). It retained a held-out score of 0.578559, with gate improving from 0.528571 to 0.644066. This run generated a different evaluator from the earlier exploratory run used in the tutorial, so their scores are not directly comparable.

CI follow-up: Docker dependency installation failed because the memory-graph lockfile pinned Tsinghua mirror URLs returning HTTP 403 for websockets 16.1.1. Normalize that lockfile to PyPI/pythonhosted URLs, preserving all 29 package versions and artifact hashes. A fresh no-cache Python 3.12 frozen install and a locked project install succeeded. Broad local pytest collected live-Neo4j cases without a configured server (95 passed, 78 fixture errors); this does not establish integration success. Full Docker validation remains with CI because Docker is unavailable locally.

items.author: Thibaultjaigu
items.body:
Users who route through Requesty currently have to set it up as a custom OpenAI compatible provider by hand. This adds it as a built-in preset alongside OpenRouter, with the same shape: OpenAI chat completions, `GET /models` discovery, and a models.dev mapping for catalog facts and prices.

## Preset
`packages/schema/src/model-provider-presets.ts` gets a `requesty` entry right after OpenRouter: base URL `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, `apiVariant: "openai"`, `modelDiscovery: "openai-models"`, docs `https://docs.requesty.ai`, key page `https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys`. `ModelProviderPresetId` in `model-provider.ts` gains `"requesty"`. The wizard and settings UI read the preset list, so nothing else changes there. Requesty is not made a default anywhere.

## models.dev mapping
models.dev publishes a `requesty` provider whose `api` is `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, so the host check in `pricesApplyToPreset` accepts its prices for this preset. It is mapped after OpenRouter, in the aggregator block, so first publish wins still hands capability facts to the vendor listings. The ordering test in `packages/model/src/models-dev.test.ts` now counts `requesty` as an aggregator so a misplaced insert would fail it.

## How to test
Pick Requesty in the connect wizard, paste a key from https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys, and choose a listed model such as `openai/gpt-4o-mini` or `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`. For EU routing, edit the base URL to `https://router.eu.requesty.ai/v1`.

## Validation
Run on macOS arm64 at ae150eb, with deps installed only for `@sciencediscovery/model` and its workspace dependencies.
- `pnpm typecheck` in `packages/schema` and `packages/model`: clean.
- `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`: OK, 276 package source files checked.
- Package unit tests with `node --test "src/**/*.test.ts"`: schema 12 passed / 0 failed, model 45 passed / 0 failed (including "every aggregator mapping sits after every vendor mapping"). These files are tagged `os:linux`, so on macOS I ran them with `process.platform` reported as linux; nothing else was changed.
- Live check through the package's own code: `listProviderModels` with the preset's `baseUrl` and discovery strategy returned 762 models including `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, and `streamModelTurn` with the preset's protocol and variant streamed a reply from `openai/gpt-4o-mini` with usage reported.
- Not run: `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` and `apps/web` tests. The UT and E2E layers need a bubblewrap sandbox on Linux, which this macOS host does not have.

## E2E user journeys
BLOCKED on this host (no Linux sandbox for the local stack). The change adds one entry to a list the connect wizard already renders, and the live check above covers the provider's discovery and chat path. Happy to add or rerun a journey if you want one for this.

## Release
Release category: release:feature (label pending a maintainer, I cannot apply labels)
User impact: Requesty appears as a provider preset in the model connect wizard.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Disclosure: I work at Requesty. Happy to adjust anything to match project conventions.

A subagent Resume action could fail with an internal server error after the user stopped its Session, because the global wake gate remained closed. Resuming a child now atomically reopens both the Session and child gates, allowing retained notices to be delivered without replaying stopped work.

## Validation

The UI removed the resume controls without an error, and the actual resume endpoint returned HTTP 200. The historical child had already failed before context persistence, so no model turn was replayed; this preserves the intended no-replay behavior.

User impact: Resuming a stopped subagent also restores its Session wake gate instead of failing with an internal server error.

items.author: wyhohyw
items.body:
This PR adds an opt-in, user-perspective JiuwenSwarm → `antibody-design` Skill → Ascend NPU journey, alongside the lower-level mocked NPU binding test. It depends on Skill backport PR #159; duplicate Skill PR #167 was closed.

## User journey

A fresh Project/Session is created with a live model and selected 131 Runner. The driver uploads the user's two PDBs and sends a high-level request through the public Session Runs API. It does not invoke any model script, choose a Python environment, or preseed model assets. The real Agent must load the Skill, inspect/select a managed environment, push inputs, perform first-use preparation and validation, run RFdiffusion → ProteinMPNN → Protenix → screening on NPU, pull results, declare report/CSV/CIF Artifacts, and explain the result. The test observes automatic wake Runs, committed execution receipts, nonempty remote and local stage files, completed transfers, and final Artifacts. It never resubmits an accepted user Run; a pipeline retry is accepted only after the preceding execution has a confirmed, committed failure. Any `unknown`/unconfirmed execution fails the test.

The real case is tagged `npu:required`, `model:real`, `status:external`, collected but deselected by ordinary PR CI until gated NPU hardware exists. The mocked binding/ST case remains for CI.

## Real-hardware verification (2026-09-24)

- **Full-Agent E2E: PASS (1/1)** on a fresh Project `9df41ef6-e2ea-4096-8e3a-6f8f5783e546`, Session `fb3dbdac-e218-40d5-a50c-565167421e4e`, initial user Run `a62cd447-a1e6-4570-8ddc-de3937edb97d`. The Agent loaded `antibody-design` itself, selected a managed environment, pushed inputs, and completed first-use preparation `74864a72-89e7-475d-af6e-ebf34495deaf` and validation with committed zero-exit receipts. One NPU pipeline Execution `a91eb590-1457-491a-977e-be73e98ba73c` finished `completed / committed / exitCode=0` on the selected remote Runner. RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN, Protenix, and screening each produced files. Report, CSV, and CIF were transferred to the Session, declared as Artifacts, and explained by the Agent across the original and an automatic wake Run.
- The full live submission used the test driver at `9afed0fa`; the final `ae556055` driver passed by **read-only observation of the same Run**, after fixing a test-only assertion that had incorrectly required three `declare_artifact` tool calls even though the Agent legitimately declares multiple Artifacts in one call. No extra NPU job was submitted for that verification. The final Agent response also names the report, CSV, and CIF. The WSL product source snapshot was labelled `89a3ac7c` and included the Skill backport.
- Earlier fresh full-Agent Run `8d3814fa-f681-4957-a647-a55c81ac06e8` is **not a pass**: first-use preparation `4eb49ef9-8c60-4708-8996-9db8fec44500` became `unknown/unconfirmed` after `fetch failed`. A first pipeline attempt then had a confirmed Runner workspace-snapshot `ENOENT` on a transient MindScience `__pycache__` file; the Agent recovered and its later NPU pipeline/output delivery succeeded, but the preparation receipt remained unconfirmed. This is a real stability risk to address separately, not a result hidden by the passing rerun.
- The older prepared-environment NPU Run `c1ba1acc-2968-417f-8714-7947ee3e1b32` is lower-level evidence only, not the full-Agent E2E result.
- `node --check`, CI contract, E2E metadata (0 errors, 11 pre-existing legacy warnings), and diff whitespace checks passed locally. The previous CI run had ST, UT, Docker, both binary builds and CLA passing; the latest push starts a fresh CI run, so its final state is not yet claimed. The hardware case is intentionally deselected in CI.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`
User impact: no runtime code change; adds regression coverage for the complete Agent-to-NPU workflow.
Compatibility: merge Skill backport PR #159 before this PR.

- Add English and Chinese Agent Team overviews based on the `science-research-team` workflow and its analysis/review/report roles.
- Add an Idea Tree walkthrough for designing catalysts to degrade pollutants in water.
- Add an Agent Team walkthrough for sepsis immune-feature correlation analysis and hierarchical clustering, including the supplied example figures and links to the BiomniBench-DA task instructions and original data.

## Validation

Validated commit: `36040e200982f5be5132789a7fb68565ad1ad384`.

- `pnpm docs:check`: PASS — 94 Markdown files linted, 0 issues; local links and image targets checked across all 94 files.

Not applicable to this change: only documentation and illustrative images are changed; no user-observable runtime path is modified. This does not count the blocked full CI E2E layer as passed.

<!-- bot0-gitcode-native-export -->

Paired: [GitHub #114](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/114) ↔ [GitCode !167](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/merge_requests/167)

/kind feature

---

## 这个 PR 做了什么 / 为什么需要

把从 Git 仓库导入第三方 Skills 的三步手工流程（粘贴 URL → 扫描 → 创建 draft → 每个 draft 单独 publish，共 80+ 次点击 / 40 个 skill）改成一键流：一次扫描 + 一个确认按钮 + 单次原子 commit。

新加端点 `POST /api/skill-review-drafts/bulk-publish-git` 一次把 N 个 Git draft 打包成一个 SkillLibrary version；UI 上配套 Quick Import 开关、Presets 下拉（LRU 10）、确认 modal。

测试中修复了用户报告的问题：用 40-skill 仓库导入后搜索框看不到 — 根因是 bulk 端点之前只写 library 不写 managed catalog，把 library 变成"只写不读"。修复方案是 bulk commit 后同步到 managed，library 失败时自动回滚 managed；批量上限从 50 提到 200 以容纳 K-Dense-AI（90 个候选）等大仓库。

---

## 这个 PR 修复的 issue

无独立 issue — 用户在 Settings → Skills 页面实测发现。

---

## 测试计划与结果

**单元测试（pass/total）：**
- `packages/schema` 14/14：provenance.metadata 兼容老 payload + bulk 请求/响应形状稳定
- `services/api` 22/22 涉及 skills 的测试，其中 bulk-import 新增 4 个：happy path、filter 模式、library 失败回滚、managed sync 校验
- `services/api` 2/2 新 HTTP 测试：seeded drafts、404 idempotence、空批 / built-in 校验
- `apps/web` 813/813：bulk-import flow 端到端、presets LRU、ButtonSemantics 新 dialog-actions 行

**端到端（手动）：**
- 起服务后 `Settings → Skills → Import → Git repository`
- 粘贴 `https://github.com/google-deepmind/science-skills/tree/main/skills` → 扫描出 40 候选
- 打开 Quick Import 开关 → 候选清单折叠，显示 "Import 40 new from science-skills @ 68832757"
- 点击按钮 → modal 列出 40 个 checkbox（4 个 invalid 默认不勾选）+ "Cancel on conflict" 勾选框（默认 ON）
- 切换到 filter 取消 ON → Confirm → 36 个 skill 出现在 Project Skills library
- 搜索框输入 `academy-guide` → 命中、点击进入 Explorer

**真实大仓库验证（K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills，90 个候选）：**
- 之前因上限 50 报错 `Select between 1 and 50` → 提升到 200 后顺利通过

**类型检查 / 构建：** 4 个受影响包（schema、specialist、web、api）clean

---

## 自检

+ - [ ] **设计**：方案已在 [plan](file:///home/zhy/.claude/plans/elegant-watching-clock.md) 记录，核心偏离（managed sync、bulk 限额）已在提交说明里交代
+ - [ ] **测试**：UT 覆盖新方法、新端点、新 UI 路径；新增测试随本 PR 一并上库
+ - [ ] **验证**：上文列出每层测试结果 + 端到端手动验证 + 真实大仓库（90 个候选）通过
+ - [ ] **接口**：新增 `POST /api/skill-review-drafts/bulk-publish-git`，新增 schema 类型 `BulkPublishGitSkillReviewDraftsRequest/Response/SkippedDraft`，均为 additive（`SkillVersionProvenance.metadata?` 也是 optional）
- - [ ] **文档**：未涉及官网文档修改

<!-- Special notes for reviewers -->
<!-- + - [ ] 是否导致无法前向兼容 -->
<!-- + - [ ] 是否涉及依赖的三方库变更 -->

items.body:
<!-- bot0-gitcode-native-export -->

Paired: [GitHub #77](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/77) ↔ [GitCode !154](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/merge_requests/154)

**What type of PR is this?**
/kind task

---

**What does this PR do / why do we need it**:

基于 `origin/main`（`425e4219`，已含 #137）从零实测 Docker Compose 部署：仓库自带 `Dockerfile` 冷构建、起栈、健康检查、浏览器登录、沙箱探针、同机多实例都能跑通，但新用户按现有文档会在几处卡住，文档也没有完整列出可配置的环境变量和常见问题。本 PR 把 Docker 部署指南重写成从构建到浏览器登录的完整步骤，补齐变量表与 FAQ，修一处 Compose 转发缺口，并把 Docker 分发路径纳入 GitHub Actions 守护。

1. **部署指南（中英同步）**：Docker 节改为「前置条件 → 准备配置与数据目录 → 构建 → 启动并确认健康 → 浏览器连接 → 配置模型」五步，之后是日常管理表、数据目录、多实例、环境变量、沙箱要求、常见问题（16 条）与限制。实测发现并写进文档的四个坑：bind mount 目录不先 `mkdir -p` 时 Docker 以 root 建目录，入口以「目录不可写」退出——多实例命令原来缺这一步，照抄必失败；日志里的登录链接端口固定是容器端口 4310，改了 `SCIENCE_AGENT_PUBLISH_PORT` 后要替换；首次启动会在后台创建 starter Python 环境（约 2 GB、需访问 conda-forge），不是卡住；镜像不含 evolve 与 memory-graph 边车，这两项功能在 Docker 中不可用。
2. **环境变量分层**：编排层只被 Compose 读取（`COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_IMAGE`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_DATA_HOST_DIR`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_UID` / `GID`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_PUBLISH_HOST` / `PORT`），容器层经 `environment` 块逐个转发，镜像层由 `Dockerfile` 固定。配置参考的 Docker 表按此拆分并补齐；未转发的变量（如 `HTTP_PROXY`）说明用 `docker-compose.override.yml` 追加。
3. **Compose 转发缺口**：配置参考把 `SCIENCE_AGENT_USAGE_EXCHANGE_RATE*` 四个键和 `SCIENCE_AGENT_MICROMAMBA_BASE_URL` 列为 Docker 变量，但 `docker-compose.yml` 都没有转发，设了静默无效（与 #137 修的上下文变量同类）。四个汇率键改为转发并加入 `.env.docker.example`，空值等于内置默认（`config.ts` 的解析函数对空串返回默认值）；micromamba 镜像 URL 从 Docker 表删除——镜像已内置并播种固定版本，运行期不下载。
4. **deploy skill**：同步补上述坑与对应的排障行。
5. **GitHub Actions `docker` job**：与 `binary` 并列的分发类门禁。真实 `docker compose build`（刻意不用缓存，冷构建才是用户的首次构建）→ 按指南首启顺序起栈 → 等 `/health` → 断言部署契约：容器名由 Compose 项目名派生、`/health` 同时报告 API 与 bubblewrap runner、Compose 健康检查到达 `healthy`、`.env.docker.example` 的键到达容器环境、micromamba 播种在文档路径、容器内探针通过 → 失败时上传容器日志 → `down`。job 不预先放宽宿主 `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns`：容器靠自己的 `security_opt` 取得沙箱能力，探针本身就是判据。起栈步骤按指南复制 `.env.docker.example` 并写入执行用户的 uid/gid：托管 runner 不是 uid 1000，否则容器写不进它刚创建的 bind mount；没有 `.env` 时所有转发键为空，「键到达容器」的断言也只会失败。构建期硬依赖 `https://models.dev/api.json`（`model-catalog` 阶段 `test -s`），该站点不可达时 job 会红，job 注释写明先看失败 stage。

提交：

- `3413fa99` fix(docker): forward the usage exchange-rate settings into the container
- `6337b67d` docs(deploy): walk a Docker user from build to a signed-in browser
- `581861c8` ci(github): build and exercise the product image on every change
- `5b2a14f6` ci(github): start the Docker job from the documented .env as the runner user

---

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
无对应 Issue。

---

**Test Plan and Test result：What scenarios were tested, and what were the verification results（Function, performance, reliability, etc.）**：

被测提交：`5b2a14f6`（基于 `origin/main` `425e4219`；对当前 `origin/main` `e79fd693` 用 `git merge-tree` 检查无冲突，改动文件互不重叠）。三层在该提交的干净 worktree 上执行。

| 检查 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| `pnpm ci:ut` | passed，exit 0，272 s（干净 worktree，14 个 outcome 全部 exit 0：install / uv sync ×2 / build / architecture:check / typecheck / ci:selftest / binary:test / workspace test / paper / gateway / memory-graph / evolve / runner）。node --test 合计 **2676 pass / 0 fail / 8 skipped**（其中 services/api 902、services/runner 245（5 skipped）、services/launcher 107）；paper `Ran 2 tests OK`、gateway `Ran 26 tests OK`、memory-graph pytest 83 passed / 77 skipped、evolve pytest 316 passed；`Architecture boundaries OK (275 package source files checked)` |
| `pnpm ci:st` | passed，22 s：`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`、`pnpm build`、`test/api/run_m1_smoke.sh` 三步 exit 0；`Agent loop smoke PASS: first-step tools + native loop + streaming model transport + real tool round-trip + multi-turn history verified.` |
| `pnpm ci:e2e`（mocked 浏览器子集） | passed，7.8 min：41 条发现，**39 passed / 0 failed / 2 skipped**。2 条 skipped 与本 PR 无关且在 `origin/main` 上相同：`journey-prepare-environment` J3 被该层自身的 `SCIENTIFIC_ENVS=0` 判为 BLOCKED；`literature-review`「Connector 未启用时的失败反馈」在仓库里是 `test.fixme` |
| `pnpm architecture:check` | Dockerfile 构建上下文测试 9/9 通过；`Architecture boundaries OK (275 package source files checked)` |
| `docker compose config -q` | 通过；4 个汇率键出现在渲染结果中 |
| GitHub `docker` job 本地回放 | 按 step 名从 `ci.yml` 提取正文原样执行（`SD_PORT=4410`）：Build / Start / Wait / Check / Report / Collect / Stop 全部 exit 0，输出 `deployment contract OK` |
| 托管 runner 的 uid 模拟 | 以 `SCIENCE_AGENT_UID=1001`、`SCIENCE_AGENT_GID=127`（容器内无 passwd 条目）起栈：2 s 健康、Compose `healthy`、容器内探针通过、`SCIENCE_AGENT_CONTEXT_MODE` 到达容器 |

`docker` job 尚未在 GitHub Actions 上真跑过；首跑需确认冷构建时长在 `timeout-minutes: 60` 内、托管 runner 磁盘容得下构建层、托管 runner 的 AppArmor 策略下容器内探针通过（本机 Ubuntu 24.04、该 sysctl 为 1 时通过）。

---

**E2E user journeys**

总判定：**PASS**
被测 SHA：`5b2a14f6`（镜像由本分支的 `Dockerfile` 构建；本 PR 不改 `Dockerfile`）
界面：Docker Compose 本地栈 + 浏览器（仓内固定 Playwright，Chromium）

| 场景 | 预期 | 实际 |
|---|---|---|
| 仓库 `Dockerfile` 冷构建 `docker compose build --no-cache` | 成功 | EXIT 0，128 s，镜像 1.77 GB |
| `mkdir -p data && docker compose up -d`，然后 `/health` | API 与 runner 均 ok，Compose healthy | 3 s 内 200，`status=ok`、`runner.status=ok`、`sandbox=bubblewrap`；40 s 时 `healthy` |
| 日志里的登录链接（端口替换为发布端口）在浏览器打开 | 令牌保存到浏览器、地址栏清除、进入工作台 | 通过：localStorage 有令牌、`location.hash` 为空、无连接弹窗 |
| 直接打开首页，在连接引导粘贴令牌 | 引导可见；错令牌被拒；正确令牌保存 | 引导含「Open to sign in」；错令牌显示「本地服务访问令牌被拒绝」；正确令牌保存后 localStorage 有令牌 |
| 鉴权 | 无令牌 401，有令牌 200 | `/api/projects` 401 / 200 |
| 沙箱 | 文档探针通过，沙箱有独立 procfs | 通过；`--unshare-pid --proc /proc` 下只见 PID 1、2 |
| 首启 starter Python 环境 | 后台自动建成 | 约 4 min 后 `runner.scientificEnvs.startersReady=true`，`./data` 1.9 GB |
| 同机第二实例（文档命令，先 `mkdir -p data-b`） | 独立容器、网络、数据目录 | `…-b` @4420 2 s 健康，第一实例不受影响；不先建目录时 Docker 以 root 建目录、入口退出——即文档新增那一步的依据 |
| uid 错配 | 立即退出并提示 | `The data directory /app/data is not writable by uid 1001, gid 1001.` |
| 端口冲突 | 明确报错 | `Bind for 127.0.0.1:4410 failed: port is already allocated` |
| 改 `.env` 后 `docker compose up -d` | 自动重建容器，新键到达 | 4 个汇率键出现在容器 `env` |

验证在非默认端口 4410 / 4420 进行以避开本机已有实例，其余步骤与文档一致。

登录链接打开后进入工作台：

![登录链接自动登录后的首页](https://raw.gitcode.com/user-images/assets/10597680/655dd9bd-4eaa-42e1-80a1-b8ddab3572fd/web-signin-url.png 'web-signin-url.png')

连接引导中粘贴令牌：

![连接引导中粘贴令牌](https://raw.gitcode.com/user-images/assets/10597680/9fac0bc3-bdde-4f65-9381-f34b6aa738a5/web-manual-paste.png 'web-manual-paste.png')

---

---

**基线更新（合入前 rebase）**

开 PR 时 head 为 `5b2a14f6`（基线 `425e4219`）。合入前已线性 rebase 到当时最新 `origin/main` `e79fd693`。最终 head：`16cf823e`。

- 上游增量 5 个提交：记忆图谱本地后端与会话卡片/徽章，与本 PR 的 Docker 文档、Compose 转发、GitHub `docker` job 无调用链交集。`docs/*/reference/configuration.md` 两边都改了，但上游只在本地模式表加了 2 行 memory-graph 变量，本 PR 改 Docker 表，rebase 无冲突。
- `git range-diff 425e4219..5b2a14f6 origin/main..16cf823e` 四条提交全部 `=`，任务补丁语义未变。
- 最终 head 上的低成本核对：`docker compose config -q` 通过；四个汇率键仍在渲染结果中；`pnpm architecture:check` 17/17；配置参考同时保留 memory-graph 新键与 Docker 表。
- 完整三层与 CodeArts 全绿是在 `5b2a14f6` 上取得的，不得把旧 SHA 冒充最终 head 的实测。rebase 后 CodeArts 会再跑一轮。

**Self-checklist**:（**请自检，在[ ]内打上x，我们将检视你的完成情况，否则会导致pr无法合入**）

+ - [ ] **设计**：PR对应的方案是否已经经过Maintainer评审，方案检视意见是否均已答复并完成方案修改

+ - [x] **验证**：PR描述信息中是否已包含对该PR对应的Feature、Refactor、Bugfix的预期目标达成情况的详细验证结果描述

Paired: [GitHub #4](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/4) ↔ [GitCode !104](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/merge_requests/104)

**What type of PR is this?**

  /kind feature

  本 PR 接入 `/idea-tree` 完整执行流程，支持主 Agent 创建探索树、派发设计与评估 Subagent、
  回传评分和 insight，并在页面查看树结构与节点结果。树状态使用本地文件持久化，无需 Neo4j。

  ### 主要变更

  1. **提取 Tree / Node 基础结构**
     - 在 Python 中定义基础节点及树查询能力，由 IdeaTree 和 PuctTree 分别继承。
     - 共用节点身份、父子关系以及节点、子节点和祖先查询。
     - 节点添加、状态更新和搜索策略由各自子类实现，比如没有引入统一的 add-node 接口, idea-tree 和 puct-tree 有各自独立的更新逻辑和增加方式。
     - PUCT 仅调整继承关系及基础字段归属，保留原有搜索、评分、访问计数和引擎调度逻辑, 没有对其原有功能造成影响。

  2. **实现 Idea Tree 的 Python 状态管理与本地持久化**
     - 在 Python 中实现节点操作、执行领取、结果提交、失败重试和 insight 回传。
     - 按项目和会话将完整树状态保存到 `idea-trees/<projectId>/<sessionId>/state.json`，使
     用临时文件与原子替换完成写入。
     - TypeScript 层负责 Agent 工具接入和 Python 服务调用，页面图结构由树状态派生。
     - Idea Tree 不再依赖 Neo4j, 完成了与 Neo4j的解耦；项目其他 Memory Graph 功能保持原有实现。
  
  3. **接通 Agent 与 Subagent 执行流程**
     - 提供 `/idea-tree` 入口及设计、评估、聚合相关 skill。
     - 主 Agent 负责探索编排，现有 Subagent 运行时执行具体任务，Python 树服务负责状态管理
     与操作约束。
     - 将工作流配置传入实际模型请求，支持评分与 insight 回传。
     - 普通文本继续未完成任务时，保留对应树工具、执行器和配置；树完成后恢复普通会话模式。
     - 支持取消后复用原树和原叶节点重试，并记录新的执行 attempt。

  4. **补充页面与服务接入**
     - 新增 Idea Tree 配置、树视图及节点详情，关联 Subagent 执行和产物。
     - 支持页面刷新后重新读取树状态与结果。
     - 修复启动脚本中 Memory Graph 和 Evolve 健康检查的端口读取，使其使用配置值。

  5. **验证截图**
  ![image.png](https://raw.gitcode.com/user-images/assets/10597680/9449699e-f848-45d9-a9f9-a9fffafcc65b/image.png 'image.png')
  ![image.png](https://raw.gitcode.com/user-images/assets/10597680/66f37432-f35f-440c-a064-0fc8a581d4a9/image.png 'image.png')
  
  ### 验证结果

  <!-- 提交前补充验证截图及说明：完整执行、树详情与刷新、取消后继续。 -->

  **Self-checklist**:（**请自检，在[ ]内打上x，我们将检视你的完成情况，否则会导致pr无法合
  入**）

  + - [x] **设计**：PR对应的方案是否已经经过Maintainer评审，方案检视意见是否均已答复并完成
  方案修改
  + - [x] **测试**：PR中的代码是否已有UT/ST测试用例进行充分的覆盖，新增测试用例是否随本PR
  一并上库或已经上库
  + - [x] **验证**：PR描述信息中是否已包含对该PR对应的Feature、Refactor、Bugfix的预期目标
  达成情况的详细验证结果描述
  + - [x] **接口**：是否涉及对外接口变更，相应变更已得到接口评审组织的通过，API对应的注释
  信息已经刷新正确
  + - [ ] **文档**：是否涉及官网文档修改，如果涉及请及时提交资料到Doc仓

## Follow-up update — 2026-09-23

This update adds the pending follow-up commits to the same personal-fork PR, rather than opening a duplicate PR. Target remains `feat/jiuwenswarm`; related #107 and #136. The validation in this section supersedes earlier local results below; historical real-model results are retained for context, not presented as validation of the latest head.

### Added scope

- Isolate shared MCP request cancellation/transport failures and add bounded, credential-conscious boundary/model-argument diagnostics. Consolidate the per-run deadline compatibility change into the version-pinned transport patch; verify patch installation is repeatable.
- Add configurable per-parent subagent concurrency (1–10, default 10) in system settings, with FIFO waiting, cancellation and lifetime-scoped permits. A deployment can set 2 without changing the product default.
- Wire real model transport/text/thinking/tool-argument progress to the owning run's idle watchdog. Preserve the hard whole-run deadline; sibling activity and unowned default-route housekeeping do not renew another run.
- Enforce child model-turn limits at request admission, before calling the provider, instead of inferring turns from UI events/tool-result counts. Keep the existing `timed_out` + `Subagent exceeded maxTurns=...` lifecycle contract. Exclude explicit housekeeping and the pinned Swarm compaction instruction; unknown future compaction prompts count conservatively as task calls. This prompt compatibility predicate is not a security boundary.
- Reject HTML/empty content masquerading as a PDF before publishing download completion. Check only a bounded 1 KiB header; full PDF parsing remains a separate extraction operation. Other artifact formats retain their behavior.
- Expand Mock literature coverage to source fallback, governed download/extraction, tool-output paging, real Swarm compaction, artifact isolation/reload, child budgets/cancellation and recovery. Add a provider-503 → cancel → healthy same-session/tool-backed run.
- Include the five stratified DeepResearchBench real cases and real custom Specialist/MCP/team signoff case, with opt-in record retention. Real evaluations remain manual and are not a PR gate.

### Latest verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Node Swarm agent/model gateway/download/subagent lifecycle regressions | 111 passed, 0 skipped |
| Python Adapter suite | 212 passed, 9 skipped: 7 opt-in live gateway scenarios and 2 real-LLM cases |
| Research model + literature-source fixture tests | 8 passed |
| Version-pinned Swarm/SDK compatibility and MCP boundary tests | 51 passed |
| FIFO subagent pool / UI settings draft tests | 3 passed / 1 passed |
| Actual Swarm + Mock LLM/source browser E2E | **20 passed, 0 skipped; 7.1 minutes; one worker** |
| Artifact manager and API builds | Passed |
| Documentation lint/links and CI catalog validation | Passed |

The 20 browser cases use the actual Swarm, Adapter, API, Runner and PDF extractor; only external model/source transports are scripted. They are not evidence of real-LLM research quality, a DRB score, or long-duration memory stability. The formerly failing LR-04 now proves the second child model request never reaches the model; LR-11 HTML now fails before completion.

Coverage details and reproduction prerequisites: `test/benchmarks/research-team/mock-coverage.md` and `jiuwen_swarm/README.md`. The existing research Mock gate remains enabled. **The complete new 20-case suite requires the dedicated offline-source fixture, exclusive Swarm instance and compaction configuration; it is not claimed to run in full in the default PR gate.** No real-provider credentials, raw private traces or local service configuration are committed. Latest CI results must be checked separately.

### Remaining boundaries

- A historical Swarm management-interface timeout was not reproduced by the new recovery case. Its initiating cause remains unproven; a passing controlled recovery test does not establish that the historical incident is fixed.
- No complete six-case real-LLM rerun or RACE/FACT quality score is claimed for this head. The interrupted DRB-59 run is not counted as successful.
- No new Swarm source patch was needed for the latest idle/model-turn/PDF fixes; the PR as a whole still includes the earlier version-pinned Swarm compatibility patches.
- This remains a source-checkout validation. Packaged binary/Docker compatibility, broader resource stability, and dashboard work remain outside these local results.

---

## Summary

Repair the Swarm-backed literature research path: specialist children receive their MCP tools, bind their own model connection, return explicit results/errors, and let the parent continue to a persisted report.

Targets `feat/jiuwenswarm` from the personal fork `zy95-12/sciencediscovery`. Related: #107, #136. Native Swarm delegation reuse remains a separate design discussion in #141.

## Changes and boundaries

- Retain **ScienceDiscovery `task` orchestration + Swarm execution** for main and child agents. When `subagents=task`, hide the native spawn/wait/list/send-input/close/resume tools from actual LLM requests, override generic native-delegation guidance, and reject stale native tool calls. Swarm search/fetch remain available.
- Bind a private model connection to each run/session using the real model name rather than per-run global model aliases/hot reloads. Forward bindings in stream/non-stream paths, allow idle-session rebinding, and reject active replacement. Preserve run/agent identity in credential-free lifecycle logs.
- Preserve startup and runtime errors, initial/resumed stream correlation and output ownership. Require an explicit terminal result: EOF/cancellation/failed status must not become successful completion.
- Keep MCP catalog refresh and child tool failures isolated; give the platform MCP transport a stable lifecycle owner and configured deadlines instead of competing wrappers/read timeouts. No automatic side-effect replay.
- Forward tool-call streaming progress, normalize model SSE output, and make child artifact handoff/provenance available to the parent.
- Carry six version-pinned, reviewable compatibility patches under `jiuwen_swarm/patches/workswarm0.2.6/`, plus regressions and setup/diagnostic documentation.
- Add/update a gate-enabled mocked research journey and an opt-in real DRB-59 browser journey, pinned upstream RACE/FACT evaluation support, and per-attempt result records. Research strategy, child count and source count are not prescribed by the benchmark prompt.

Merged the latest target branch and resolved the `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh` conflict: source installs apply compatibility patches before virtualenv synchronization; the target branch's preinstalled path and instance initialization remain intact. The real validation below uses the source checkout, not packaged Docker/binary distributions; these distribution channels still need patch compatibility validation before claiming support for this run contract.

## Mock E2E is a PR gate; real E2E is manual only

`test/swarm-research-mocked.spec.ts` is included in the default mocked PR gate; the CI Swarm stack already enables its platform-task prerequisite. Only `test/deepresearchbench-swarm.spec.ts` is excluded unless **`E2E_RESEARCH=1`**. PR workflows do not set that variable. Real tests additionally require the real project and live credentials. Fast unit regressions also remain in normal CI.

Verified by test discovery: the default mocked list contains the Swarm research mock case and excludes the real case; explicit real opt-in discovers DRB-59. No scheduled benchmark/dashboard workflow was added.

Manual runs against an isolated, configured Swarm stack:

```bash
E2E_SWARM_TASK=1 npm --prefix .e2e run test:mocked -- swarm-research-mocked.spec.ts
E2E_RESEARCH=1 E2E_SWARM_TASK=1 E2E_DRB_EVALUATION=off npm --prefix .e2e run test:real -- deepresearchbench-swarm.spec.ts
```

See `jiuwen_swarm/README.md` and `test/benchmarks/deepresearchbench/README.md` for auth, generator/Judge configuration and full evaluation. Evaluation defaults to `full`; `off` is an explicit integration-only diagnostic mode, not a quality pass.

## Validation

### Latest real run — September 23

**GLM-5.2 + actual Swarm + browser: 1 passed.** Same DRB-59 bird-migration question as the preceding failed attempt. No fixed delegation count/search-depth prompt limits.

| Observation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Actual delegation | Four platform `task` children; all completed |
| Child branches | Magnetic, celestial, olfactory/landmark, navigation disturbances |
| Recorded child turns | 9 / 25 / 16 / 15 |
| MCP activity | Successful PubMed / Europe PMC calls; child artifacts declared |
| Parent continuation | Continued research after child results and declared final report |
| Persisted report | `deepresearchbench-59.md`, 5,428 words, 30 headings, 50 distinct URL strings |
| Browser assertions | Visible artifact/preview, basic report structure, reload persistence and final handoff passed |
| Generation duration | 1,011,856 ms (~16.9 minutes) |
| Total browser test | ~23.8 minutes |
| RACE / FACT | Disabled for this run; **no quality score claimed** |

Browser validation was slowed by cgroup memory reclaim; the browser soft/hard limits were raised from 650/850 MiB to 1000/1100 MiB after checking host capacity. Assertions were unchanged; no OOM was observed. This affects timing comparisons. Raw traces remain private because they may contain credentials/research content; test services were stopped afterwards.

The earlier run failed because native subagent tools leaked into the task-mode toolset and native activity did not reset the platform idle timer. That failure is not hidden: the isolation fix addresses the task path; native-child progress forwarding remains outside this PR.

### Automated regressions

- After target-branch merge: API build, 86 affected Node tests, 190 adapter tests (9 skipped: 7 opt-in live Gateway scenarios and 2 real-LLM tests), 72 engineering/CI self-tests, documentation checks, shell syntax and compatibility patch reverse-applicability checks passed.
- Delegation isolation validation: 72 Node tests and 71 adapter tests passed.
- Earlier broader validation on this change series: 189 adapter tests passed / 9 skipped; 167 affected Node tests; 23 patched Swarm/SDK regressions; workspace typecheck, architecture boundaries, native hermetic ST smoke passed.
- Actual Swarm + mocked LLM browser journey: 1 passed (44.2 s), covering child error recovery, child artifact, parent reading it, final report/UI and follow-up session rebinding. This precedes the final isolation/config-only updates.
- Evaluator unit tests: 9 passed, 1 skipped, 9 subtests passed. The skip needs an external pinned evaluator checkout; it is not counted as passing.

This is not a full repository regression run. The real E2E pass precedes the subsequent target merge/manual-collection-only changes; it was not rerun after that merge. Latest CI still needs to run on this PR head.

## Known limitations / follow-up

- arXiv returned HTTP 406; one child mixed read_tool_output query/range arguments; another used a temporary file across shell calls. All recovered or continued in the passing run; upstream availability and these ergonomics are not claimed fixed.
- Native todo tools remain visible when platform update_plan is selected. Native-child progress forwarding and full native delegation inheritance are not implemented here.
- Platform usage currently reports one invocation / 138,374 tokens for the run; this is **not a verified aggregate of all main/child requests** and must not be shown as full benchmark cost.
- No all-five-case result, official leaderboard score, or full RACE+FACT pass is claimed. A historical separate RACE run scored 47.49/100 with substituted GLM-5.2 Judge on an earlier report; it is not the score of the current passing run.
- Version-wide dashboard implementation is owned by a separate workstream. This PR supplies `benchmark-metrics.json`, exact report input and optional evaluation scorecards/usage/provenance for later ingestion; it does not implement dashboard UI, aggregation or scheduling. Missing/disabled/partial scores must not be treated as quality passes.
