## Problem and behavior

Test entry points and discovery rules did not describe the same repository coverage. This change gives local development and CI one selector/runner, loads scenario metadata from adjacent `.case.yaml` files and module discovery from `.suite.yaml`, and preserves the existing test frameworks and default `pnpm test` scope.

Browser journeys move to `test/e2e/`, standalone API journeys to `test/st/api/`, and native agent smoke tests to `test/st/agent-runtime/`. Backend API and all contract scenarios are classified as ST; E2E is reserved for browser user journeys. Shared contract replay/normalization/comparison code lives once in `test/support/contract/`, with its UT alongside it; scenarios, baselines and accepted-difference policy live in `test/st/contract/`. Recursive Node/Web discovery, asset ownership checks and source/build mapping prevent silent omissions. Issue-number filenames are replaced with scenario/object names. Only two previously approved obsolete browser declarations are retired, with reasons and the remaining disabled-connector coverage gap recorded in the migration ledger.

## Directory and layer model

- Product UT stays in the owning module; test-tooling UT stays beside its implementation in `test/support/`.
- `test/st/agent-runtime/` covers direct cross-module agent collaboration.
- `test/st/api/` covers backend service chains through HTTP; `test/st/contract/` owns HTTP/event-stream scenarios and baselines. Both L1 and L2 contracts are ST.
- `test/e2e/` contains browser user journeys. There is no separate API E2E category.
- `test/support/contract/` supplies one shared contract implementation; no scenario-specific copies of the runner or normalizer are introduced.
- API IDs are `st.api.<scenario>` and all contract IDs are `st.contract.<scenario>`. `test/support/migration.json` records the moves and prior draft IDs. Browser IDs and PR/daily membership/backend matrices are unchanged.

## Scenario naming

Use lowercase kebab-case object/behavior names, without issue numbers, `journey-` / `-journey` or `l1-` / `l2-` labels. Examples:

- `test/e2e/first-run-onboarding.spec.ts` and `.case.yaml`, ID `e2e.browser.first-run-onboarding`.
- `test/st/api/child-workspace.mjs` and `.case.yaml`, ID `st.api.child-workspace`.
- `test/st/contract/cases/run-approval-denied.case.yaml`, scenario ID `run-approval-denied`, catalog ID `st.contract.run-approval-denied`.
- `session-multi-turn` describes the former `l2-two-turns` contract scenario; `run-events.json` holds run-event scenarios.

Implementation/config filenames and IDs stay aligned. Shared browser helpers are `scenario-fixtures.ts`, `scenario-report.ts` and `browser-fixture.ts`. Module UT follows module names; Python's conventional `test_*.py` discovery remains unchanged.

Step-report validation is now explicit in YAML (`reporting: steps`) rather than inferred from a `journey-` filename; all formerly marked journeys retain this enforcement. Naming validation rejects the historical test filename prefixes/suffixes.

`namingMigration` in `test/support/migration.json` records old/new paths, catalog IDs and contract scenario IDs. Baseline keys and accepted-difference case references are renamed together; expected response payloads, scenario steps and difference predicates are unchanged. External baselines using the old IDs need the same key migration. The naming migration preserved all 92 configured entries and their policies; the subsequent real-model extension below adds daily coverage, and all 88 retained browser test identities were verified after filename mapping.

## Triggers and usage

Install with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then:

```bash
pnpm test:list --profile pr --json
pnpm test:list --profile daily --json
pnpm test:doctor --case e2e.browser.first-run-onboarding --executor jiuwenswarm
pnpm test:pr
pnpm test:daily
pnpm test --case st.api.child-workspace --executor native
pnpm test --profile full --executor both
pnpm test:check
```

- PR opened/synchronize/reopened events run the configured PR policy. Pushes to `main`/`master` and manual CI dispatch use the same policy; existing binary/Docker gates remain.
- `test-daily.yml` schedules the daily policy at **00:17 UTC / 08:17 Asia/Shanghai**, with manual dispatch also declared. Scheduled execution starts when the workflow reaches the default branch.
- PR policy has **7 required entries**: both UT tiers, native deterministic ST, and four JiuwenSwarm browser scenarios. Daily policy has **82 required entries plus 54 observational contract entries** (27 scenarios × two executor labels). These are execution entries, not framework case counts.
- YAML separates `llm.mode`, supported executors and scheduled executors. Real-model/hardware/legacy gates are never enabled by selection. PR/daily executor policy cannot be overridden on the command line.
- Nonblocking entries retain FAIL/BLOCKED/etc. and produce `passed-with-observations` when required tasks pass. Full/manual selections treat every selected entry as required.
- GitHub provisions the browser stack/JiuwenSwarm dependencies; local callers must supply the prerequisites reported by `test:doctor`. CodeArts keeps its existing compatibility command scope.

See [test/README.md](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/refactor/configured-test-harness/test/README.md) for configuration examples, gates, executor limitations and report locations. Reports distinguish PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, SKIPPED and NOT_RUN; external contract executor labels remain explicitly operator-declared.

## Configured subject models and assertions

Every case now explicitly declares `assertions.mode`: `deterministic`, `llm`, or `hybrid`. Real subject models are configured independently from judge models:

```yaml
llm:
  mode: real
  model:
    protocol: chat-completions
    baseUrlEnv: E2E_LLM_BASE_URL
    modelEnv: E2E_LLM_MODEL
    apiKeyEnv: E2E_LLM_TOKEN
assertions:
  mode: hybrid
  judge:
    model:
      protocol: chat-completions
      baseUrlEnv: E2E_JUDGE_BASE_URL
      modelEnv: E2E_JUDGE_MODEL
      apiKeyEnv: E2E_JUDGE_TOKEN
    timeoutSeconds: 60
    maxTokens: 1200
    maxInputCharacters: 24000
    rubric:
      - id: task-completion
        description: The answer and supplied artifact meet the requested task.
        threshold: 0.8
```

A model profile accepts exactly one literal `model` or `modelEnv`; each case may bind different environment names. Credentials are never stored in YAML. The initial transport is OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions; scoring requires a model supporting its temperature/max-token parameters.

Browser cases use `assessment.check(name, callback)` for configurable programmatic assertions and `assessment.submit({task, answer, artifacts, context})` for actual bounded evidence. Deterministic mode runs checks without a judge call. LLM-only mode skips those optional assertion callbacks. Hybrid mode requires at least one successful named check and all judge thresholds to pass. Ordinary framework `expect` calls remain mandatory structural/workflow guards. Never put setup/actions inside the optional assertion callback.

Judging runs only after the test body passes. Missing evidence, missing model configuration, malformed/missing/duplicate scores, low scores, HTTP errors and timeouts cannot produce PASS. There is no automatic fallback or retry. Every criterion has an explicit threshold in [0,1]. The configured input limit rejects oversized evidence rather than silently truncating it. Reports include per-attempt assessment attachments, resolved subject/judge identities, sanitized evidence, rubric, scores, reasons, usage when supplied and latency. A framework pass without required scoring evidence is rejected by the harness. Qualitative scoring does not prove numerical correctness; keep objective calculations checked programmatically.

The initial production example is `e2e.browser.model-request`: real subject + hybrid completion/delivery checks and report-quality scoring. The other two existing real-browser files retain deterministic assertions. All non-browser runners currently support deterministic assertions; unsupported scoring/runner combinations fail configuration validation explicitly.

## Daily real-model execution and setup

`test-daily.yml` invokes independent `external:none` and `external:real` jobs through the same reusable workflow. The external tag is derived from **either** a real subject or a live judge, so stub-subject/live-judge cases cannot accidentally enter the deterministic job. PR remains deterministic and receives no model secrets.

All three real-browser files run daily on both native and JiuwenSwarm as required work: six added entries. Daily now expands to **136 entries: 82 required and 54 observational contracts**. PR remains seven required entries. The real job explicitly sets `CI_ALLOW_REAL=1`; missing credentials cause required work to fail with unmet prerequisites.

Configure these repository Actions secrets for the supplied profiles:

- `E2E_LLM_BASE_URL`, `E2E_LLM_MODEL`, `E2E_LLM_TOKEN`.
- `E2E_JUDGE_BASE_URL`, `E2E_JUDGE_MODEL`, `E2E_JUDGE_TOKEN`.

Custom case-specific environment names must also be wired into the workflow. The implementation does not create secrets or choose a paid provider. Inspect with `pnpm test:list --profile daily --tag external:real --json`; with the six values exported and the isolated stack prerequisites ready, use `CI_ALLOW_REAL=1 pnpm test:daily --tag external:real`.

`literature-review` now registers/selects the configured model rather than hardcoded DeepSeek profiles; it still depends on its Skill/connector fixtures and PubMed availability. Those remaining requirements can block daily runs. Real-project Playwright traces are disabled because registration request bodies contain model keys; step screenshots and sanitized scoring evidence remain.

Local validation includes actual Playwright fixture execution against a local HTTP judge: three expected passes, three deliberate failures (native check, missing evidence, low score), three scoring requests and five assessment attachments. This verifies execution/reporting integration without calling an external model. No real-provider or complete product E2E pass is claimed: subject/judge variables were absent in the local environment during validation.

## Validation and limitations

Rebased onto `feat/jiuwenswarm` revision `9670568`, preserving its added tests, isolation changes and accepted contract differences.

- Catalog validation: **92 execution entries, 48 suites, 437 static assets**.
- Harness/contract tooling: **65 tests passed**; CI self-tests: **53 passed**; architecture: **19 passed** plus boundary validation.
- Documentation lint and links passed across 89 Markdown files.
- Pinned Playwright collection compared with the latest target: **90 upstream identities → 88 retained identities in 47 files**; exactly the two approved retirements explain the difference. This is collection, not test execution.
- Workflow YAML parsing, shell syntax and diff whitespace checks passed. Workspace-only guest packaging was checked for the YAML runtime dependency.

A full product E2E run and remote workflow execution have **not** been certified by these checks. Contract CI targets/baseline selection remain unprovisioned; their observations report BLOCKED until supplied. Existing product failures are not suppressed or fixed by this test-engineering change.

Implements #126. The issue remains the detailed scope and trigger/usage reference; merging into this feature branch does not activate default-branch scheduled runs.

Bring the shared antibody-design workflow from `main` into `feat/jiuwenswarm`. This adds sandbox NPU execution for Protenix, makes RFdiffusion installation reproducible, and adopts the same built-in skill name and persisted-ID behavior as main. JiuwenSwarm's adapter, executor, test wrapper, and documentation layout remain intact.

## Changes compared with main

Compared main `60bc099eee4e3d7da030981a7308fb8ff7d3b8f5` with JiuwenSwarm base `b255fea88cae160381c87b3618261a60d660921c`, checking patches and resulting files as well as commit ancestry.

| Main commit | Handling |
| --- | --- |
| `ac445670` — sandbox NPU execution for Protenix | Cherry-picked with original provenance. |
| `862e6604` — reproducible RFdiffusion setup | Cherry-picked with original provenance. |
| `624c3b2c` — rename the workflow to `antibody-design` | Cherry-picked; documentation follows this branch's existing directory layout. |
| `db5f47ac` — remove automatic persisted-ID migration | Cherry-picked to retain main's final behavior. |
| `b97dcbfb` — pytest project configuration | The fix already exists here in `f553e8b4`, including explicit adapter plugins. Ported the missing regression test only. |
| `04194014` — upload results from hidden directories | The workflow already includes the fix from `854267a7`. Ported the missing upload regression test only. |

E2E driver output from main `60bc099e` is already present as `b255fea8`. The repository-operation documentation change in `94de21ce` is outside this product backport.

## Validation

Candidate: `007e13e3ee9050b7e82dbcf3d8f01d24c630568a`.

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm build`: passed with Node 22.19.0.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s skills/antibody-design/scripts -p 'test_*.py'`: 24 passed.
- `pnpm ci:selftest`: 13 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- `pnpm test:tagged:selftest`: 47 Node tests and 8 Python tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern='Protenix|skill lifecycle APIs' services/runner/src/server.test.ts services/api/src/server.test.ts`: 6 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Covers the renamed built-in skill API and pipeline scripts.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/specialist test`: 1 passed.
- `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm docs:check`: passed; 87 Markdown files checked.
- `pnpm ci:st`: planned = executed = passed = 1; failed = skipped = 0.
- Full local `pnpm ci:ut` and `pnpm ci:e2e`: **BLOCKED before invocation**. Their existing JiuwenSwarm setup creates an instance under a fixed per-user directory outside this validation host's permitted filesystem scope. The wrapper was not bypassed and these layers are not claimed as passed. GitHub Actions must provide the remaining gates.

## E2E user journeys

**BLOCKED**, candidate `007e13e3`: the isolated JiuwenSwarm browser stack could not be started within the local filesystem boundary. The focused API/Runner tests above are regression tests, not a full E2E result. Real RFdiffusion/Protenix inference on NPU hardware has not been run here; the 24 Python tests exercise setup and validation with fixtures. Keep this PR in draft pending the remaining CI and integration validation.

## Release

Release category: `release:breaking`.

User impact: the bundled antibody workflow supports sandbox NPU execution and reproducible dependency setup. Compatibility: its built-in ID and directory change from `antibody-protenix-pipeline` to `antibody-design`; update explicit script paths and skill-ID references, and select the renamed skill where necessary. As on main, this backport does not automatically rewrite persisted old IDs.

The JiuwenSwarm branch still bundles the older antibody-protenix-pipeline Skill. This ports the previously merged GitCode #145 antibody-design workflow to this branch so an Agent can run the full RFdiffusion → ProteinMPNN → Protenix → screening pipeline through one managed sandbox NPU Shell Execution.

## Changes

- Replace the older built-in Skill with antibody-design and update its Specialist registration and affected test fixtures.
- Preserve pinned model/checkpoint preparation, managed-environment validation, the RFdiffusion MindSpore I/O patch, and same-Execution monitoring and remote output transfer.
- Keep the optional generic Host NPU Broker untouched; the antibody Skill uses the ordinary managed sandbox path.
- Mark `.patch` files LF-normalized while preserving the whitespace required by unified-diff context lines.

## Validation

- Base: `feat/jiuwenswarm` at `45717e72`; candidate: `e71e2b3d`.
- WSL Skill Python tests: 25 passed / 0 failed.
- WSL `pnpm build`: passed.
- The latest combined Skill + NPU-test candidate completed all 3495 non-root UT identities: 3491 passed, 4 failed. Three JiuwenSwarm-backed API failures match failures reproduced on the unmodified earlier base; the fourth was a type error in the separate test PR and has since been fixed. Full `pnpm typecheck` and the affected mock test now pass at the corrected combined SHA.
- ST on the corrected combined candidate: 1/1 passed. Mocked browser E2E on the clean combined candidate at `1ed585aa`: 40/44 passed, 4 failed (Skill review draft creation, model-connect layout width, Workspace Plan cards, plugin-composition Plan restore). The Skill draft failure resembles an API failure reproduced on the unmodified earlier base; the remaining browser failures have not been baseline-attributed. CI is not claimed green.
- The `ci:e2e` wrapper also reported a later `skill_tool` / `unable to open database file` error in its post-browser integration checks; investigation remains open.

## E2E user journeys

The latest `45717e72` combined candidate completed a real Ascend run: Agent Run `c1ba1acc-2968-417f-8714-7947ee3e1b32`, managed Execution `54ba4acb-d7d5-4d94-b4ac-b3814012a789`, `completed/committed/exitCode=0`, nonempty screening report/CSV transferred to the Session and declared as Artifacts. The live job started on product code at `89a3ac7c`; subsequent combined commits changed only test assertions. The corrected driver re-observed the same Run ID read-only at `9ae5fbe2` and passed 1/1; it did not replay the NPU job. Two earlier `b255fea8` attempts failed before the pipeline, demonstrating the connection/gateway instability that this test must catch.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature`
User impact: Antibody design can use the selected sandbox NPU Runner through the managed execution path.
Compatibility and migration: Existing references to the old built-in Skill ID must select `antibody-design`.

Related historical change: https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/pull/145

recent_closed_unmerged.body:
#152 added a `github` skill, the usage guide for `gh`, and made issue and pull request text on this repository English. It landed on `main` only; `feat/jiuwenswarm` still told agents that `origin` is GitCode and to default to Chinese templates. This brings that commit here unchanged.

## What it carries

The same three files as `94de21ce` on `main`, cherry-picked verbatim so a later merge of `main` finds nothing to reconcile:

This follows up on #123 (merged) with the next 51 commits of JiuwenSwarm backend integration work: prompt assembly order, tool exposure policy, task planning, approvals, skill setup, web search, trajectory recording, context compression, language sync, and sub-agent delegation.

## Prompt order
ScienceDiscovery's own product prompt comes first, JiuwenSwarm's full system prompt is kept intact and comes second, and the run contract comes last. New `SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_PROMPT` switch (`replace` restores the old behavior). Adapter debug level 2 prints the full system prompt and tool list.

## Tool exposure
By default the model uses JiuwenSwarm's own tools, and ScienceDiscovery's tools are added only where JiuwenSwarm has no equivalent capability (`SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_TOOLS=ours` switches back to the old full tool set). JiuwenSwarm's built-in host tools (bash, file read/write/edit, glob, grep, read_pdf) are hidden, with the equivalent capability going through ScienceDiscovery's sandboxed tools instead. Every tool for a run goes through one shared MCP server, named with a stable `mcp_sci_<tool>` scheme so JiuwenSwarm's permission policy can reference them. When names collide, each side's schema is kept without duplicate exposure.

## Task planning
The executor defaults to planning with JiuwenSwarm's own todo tool (`SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_PLANNING=update_plan` switches back to the old approach); CI journeys still override with `update_plan`.

## Approvals
Approval questions are judged independently per resource instead of reusing an earlier approval for the same resource. Approval cards show the call the model-facing proxy actually saw (tool name plus the concrete command/arguments).

## Skill setup
The JiuwenSwarm backend reuses JiuwenSwarm's own skill mechanism, importing the run's skills into it; ScienceDiscovery's own skill directory and `read_skill` no longer apply under JiuwenSwarm. Skill toggles are managed from the settings page and apply to every session of the run.

## Web search
JiuwenSwarm's own web search (`free_search`) and page fetch (`fetch_webpage`) are on by default, driven by the web settings page (Bocha/Serper/Perplexity keys, backend selection); settings are pushed through the adapter's `config.set` and take effect after restart. Results from JiuwenSwarm's search/fetch are recorded into the memory graph the same way ScienceDiscovery's own search is (WebPage nodes plus body text in CAS).

## Trajectory
Adds a trajectory view for JiuwenSwarm runs, recording each model call's raw input/output, tool observations, and committed steps; sub-agents stay the `task` type but are tagged with their source.

## Context compression
The compression window is now a deployment-level setting (`JIUWENSWARM_CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS`) instead of being configured per model. JiuwenSwarm's default model entry points at the adapter, and the adapter's own calls (including compression requests) are sent to whichever model the current run is using. The default model entry always sorts first in the model list, is written on startup, and is preserved when the list is trimmed (avoids JiuwenSwarm erroring on an empty model list).

## Language sync
Switching the UI language (zh/en) also sets JiuwenSwarm's `preferred_language`, including mid-session switches.

## Sub-agents
Sub-agent delegation now goes through JiuwenSwarm's own `subagent_spawn`/`subagent_wait`.

## CI
GitHub Actions' mocked E2E now runs against the JiuwenSwarm backend by default.

## Docs
Updated install/build guides, prompt ordering, tools/sandbox/approvals, skill setup, trajectory, and language sync documentation to match.

## Validation
Local `pnpm ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e` were not run for this PR — skipped at the operator's request so this PR could be opened directly and validated by remote CI (GitHub Actions) instead. Will update this description with local validation numbers if/when they're run.

## Summary

Reduce false `unknown / unconfirmed` outcomes when an already accepted remote Shell Execution has a transient Runner status observation failure. This is a bounded mitigation for #185, not a claim that the underlying transport failure or post-`unknown` reconciliation has been solved.

## Changes

- Increase the wait between retries after transient Runner status-observation failures, with bounded backoff; keep querying the original Execution ID and never resubmit the accepted command.
- Reset the consecutive-failure count after any successful Runner status observation, including a still-running result.
- Mark the local execution `unknown / unconfirmed` only after **five consecutive** retryable status failures. Preserve the underlying error code in the recorded message when available. Identity mismatches and other non-retryable errors still fail immediately.
- Keep one concise, matching status-observation note in the English and Chinese `execution-workspaces.md` pages; no separate design page.
- Add regression tests for four failures followed by success, a success that resets the counter, and five consecutive failures without command replay.

## Validation

- WSL `pnpm build`: passed.
- WSL `node --import tsx --test src/shell-executions.test.ts` in `services/api`: 10/10 passed.
- `pnpm docs:check`: passed (0 lint issues; links checked across 87 Markdown files).
- One real Agent → antibody-design Skill → Ascend NPU workflow using this candidate completed the remote pipeline with committed provenance and delivered report, CSV, and CIF artifacts, with no `unknown` execution observed. PR #168's E2E assertion was corrected to match the natural-language request; a read-only resume of that same real Run passed 1/1. **This is one successful run, not statistical proof that transient failures have been eliminated.**
- Full WSL `pnpm test`: blocked in the existing binary-release suite because `services/runner/dist/sea/linux-x64/sciencediscovery-runner` is not provisioned (`ENOENT`; 28/29 binary tests passed). The command did not reach the recursive package tests. The user explicitly requested the PR despite this environment limitation.

## Follow-up

Issue #185 tracks the still-open root-cause investigation and Runner-authoritative reconciliation after the retry threshold, API restart, or Runner reconnection. This PR intentionally does not replay or recover an execution once it is already `unknown`.

recent_merged.author: zy95-12
recent_merged.body:
## Problem and behavior
When a trajectory observer stalls, cancelling a Swarm run previously left the model gateway awaiting that observer. Once it eventually resolved, the gateway could still invoke the model client with an aborted signal. Final cleanup could also keep the cancelled run waiting for the recorder queue.

Make input/completion recording waits and final recorder draining cancellation-aware. Re-check cancellation before model dispatch. Already-started storage work remains serialized and drains/closes in its original queue; cancellation does not close storage mid-write. Normal runs still await recording and final cleanup.

## Diagnostics
Add payload-free `[recording-progress]` logs for queue waits, state/authority capture, workspace snapshots, context/step commits and final flushing. Operations pending for 30 seconds automatically log periodically without verbose tracing. Logs include operation/trajectory/request identifiers where available, elapsed time, cancellation and eventual completion/failure. Gateway diagnostics distinguish recording from upstream dispatch and response receipt. Developer documentation explains flags and limitations.

This fixes a confirmed cancellation defect, **not the unexplained historical multi-minute recording latency**. The new diagnostics are intended to identify that intermittent cause. Existing real E2E processes were not changed or restarted.

## Validation
- 123 related unit tests passed (gateway, Swarm agent, recorder/versioning, deadlines, new recording helper).
- Re-ran all 23 gateway tests after final dispatch guards: passed.
- API TypeScript build and test TypeScript checking passed.
- Replaced the gateway temporarily with the baseline implementation and ran the blocked-input regression without its new phase assertion: both streaming and non-streaming cases timed out after cancellation. Restored fix; both pass.
- Regression coverage includes late recording completion (no upstream dispatch), late rejection, cancelled final cleanup, and automatic slow-stage logs without research payloads.

recent_merged.body:
Real research runs could deliver a report but fail Playwright because of fixed filenames, word/citation counts, workflow checks or quality thresholds. Separate completion from quality across all eight opt-in research cases.

- Completion requires a completed main run and a final response referencing a readable, nonempty persisted artifact. Intermediate outputs alone cannot pass; failed/cancelled runs with final outputs remain partial. Explicit version links are read immutably.
- Remove scientific/workflow quality assertions from completion. Preserve original research prompts, DRB RACE/FACT formulas and BiomniBench expert rubrics. Quality errors, missing inputs and low scores remain visible without failing delivery. Biomni rubric evaluation is enabled by default, with an explicit off mode.
- Add the versioned TC rubric: task coverage 20, evidence 25, analysis 25, reproducibility 15, collaboration/audit 15. A read-only Judge inspects frozen artifacts and retained trajectories. Code validates artifact/version identities and computes scores from 0–4 levels. Deterministic audit-text comparison is evidence for the Judge, not a new pass/fail gate.
- Retain raw Judge responses and bounded formatting recovery; truncated/invalid responses yield an error with no score. Existing evaluation directories cannot be reused. No additional automated Harness diagnostics layer.

Validation: delivery selection tests (3), immutable-content API tests (3), TC Judge tests (7, also invoked by a tagged UT wrapper), DRB evaluator/contract tests (16 passed, including the pinned upstream pipeline with mocked Judge/fetch and one correction), Biomni evaluator tests (3), targeted TypeScript checks, E2E metadata/catalog checks, Markdown lint and collection of all 8 real cases passed. Offline evidence loading against the three retained TC runs identified the known initial audit mismatch and later exact re-audits. No new paid research runs were started for this refactor.

Quality scores are independent assessments, not proof of correctness or delivery thresholds. DRB evaluation modes and coverage must still be reported separately; Biomni uses the existing local adapter to the official rubric.

RACE response reliability: add stable criterion IDs with the `race-criterion-id-v1` output-format appendix; preserve official rubric text, weights and upstream calculation. Validate IDs and scores before restoring canonical names. Allow one structure-correction call, reject changes to existing valid judgements, retain raw/normalized responses and specific validation errors, and prevent nested outer retries. The retained DRB-59 repeat-3 response is a regression fixture: old validation rejects its abbreviated name, while an explicit ID correction preserves all 26 judgements. No runtime fuzzy matching or historical score rewriting.

Executed failing phases now record `error`; configured FACT skips record `skipped` with a reason. Completed RACE scores remain visible if FACT fails. The output-format adapter version is recorded for comparisons. The additional tagged UT wrapper and catalog/Markdown checks passed.

recent_merged.author: zy95-12
recent_merged.body:
## Problem
BiomniBench da-14-1 repeat 2 failed after three Swarm 60-second stream-idle timeouts while the model was actively generating tool arguments. At cancellation the gateway had received upstream data 2–9ms earlier and buffered 52–55KB of arguments.

The gateway correctly withheld incomplete tool arguments, but represented their progress as SSE comments. The OpenAI SDK discards those comments, so Swarm's decoded-chunk watchdog saw no progress and cancelled healthy generation.

## Change
Send a standard empty `delta` data event for each received tool-argument increment, through the existing downstream progress accounting. No partial arguments or synthetic assistant text are sent. Complete calls are released once at the finish boundary; truncated calls remain withheld. No timer-generated keepalive is introduced, so true upstream silence still times out.

Independent of PR #193 (recording cancellation), based directly on feat/jiuwenswarm.

## Validation
- 112 gateway/Swarm agent unit tests passed, including incremental-progress assertions before model completion and both complete/truncated argument cases.
- API TypeScript build and test TypeScript check passed.
- Actual gateway -> installed OpenAI SDK -> openJiuwen Model.stream parser/watchdog probe passed: a 1s argument stream survives a 0.5s idle budget, a complete call is emitted once, a truncated call never appears, and real upstream silence still times out.
- The identical full-client probe against the previous gateway fails with idle_chunk timeout despite continuous upstream increments (red/green verified).

Repeat the local integration probe with the Python environment used by Swarm (no paid model calls):
```bash
SWARM_PYTHON=/path/to/swarm/.venv/bin/python node --import tsx test/fixtures/swarm-tool-heartbeat-probe.mjs
```
The probe is optional, separate from the regular Node UT gate because it requires the Swarm Python installation. Existing real E2E processes were not modified or restarted.

recent_merged.author: zy95-12
recent_merged.body:
A child repairing a report currently receives an Artifact reference but has no editable local copy. Paging the Artifact and reconstructing it through model-generated shell commands wastes time and risks truncated tool arguments or altered content. This change lets the child copy a fixed version into its isolated workspace, edit it with suitable tools, and publish an explicit revision of the original Artifact.

- Add `materialize_artifact(artifact_id, version, path)`: stream the original bytes from CAS through the existing workspace lock, checksum validation and atomic publication path. Return metadata only; reject different existing content and unsafe paths. Identical copies can be retried.
- Extend single-file `declare_artifact` with paired `artifact_id` and `base_version_id`. Preserve Artifact identity, immutable history, citation-chip mappings and base-version provenance. Reject stale bases, preserve local edits, and deduplicate replays using a persisted tool-call publication ID.
- Make the tools available to both the parent and native-task → Swarm children. Add short editing guidance and retain materialization receipts in durable Artifact context after compression.
- Preserve existing declarations and workspace isolation. Binary/generated files use their normal editing or generation tools; no text conversion, task dependency engine or shared writable parent directory is introduced.

Validation: workspace build and typecheck; 158 focused existing/new tests plus 2 durable-context tests; three real-stack mocked E2Es (AR-01, LR-13, LR-15) passed. AR-01 edits a large Unicode report in a Swarm child, checks exact original/revised bytes and proves the import result contains no report text. Service tests cover binary bytes, restart/replay, concurrent/stale publication, preserved local edits, traversal, symlinks, cross-project access and damaged CAS content. The frozen PR plan selects AR-01 as reviewed; no gate is weakened. CI catalog check passed.

DRB-64 has been launched separately with RACE scoring, memory graph disabled, the same 60-minute agent budget and a 24 GiB memory cap. Its result is pending; no claim of improved research efficiency yet. Catalog compare-and-update relies on the existing single-process SessionStore, not a new distributed transaction scheme.



The first CI run also exposed an existing J3 activity-disclosure regression: the trace shows a successful expand click followed about 65 ms later by a terminal refresh replacing the live card with a collapsed historical card. A separate commit preserves disclosure choices during that transition and records summary clicks synchronously before native toggle/remount. Existing J3 assertions and timeouts are unchanged. The added migration assertion failed before the fix; all 857 web tests, web typecheck/build and the complete J3 mocked journey pass locally after the fix. The latest remote CI run is pending.

recent_merged.author: zy95-12
recent_merged.body:
Uncached arXiv searches in DRB-62 repeatedly returned HTTP 406, while long literature handoffs risked losing work at the end of a run. This PR changes the arXiv TLS handshake, encourages incremental artifact delivery, and adds diagnostics for research runs that stall or fail.

Changes:
- Enable `post_handshake_auth` on the certificate-verifying TLS context for arXiv searches only. Other biomedical sources retain their existing client settings.
- Suggest small batches of complete literature records, recoverable checkpoints, validation/deduplication and optional early versioned artifacts. Large child deliverables should use artifact references and concise final handoffs.
- Add opt-in arXiv HTTP diagnostics with status, timing, Retry-After, selected edge headers and a query hash; research text is not logged.
- Set DRB-58/59 generation budgets to 90/120 minutes, with separate per-case overrides and a separate evaluation budget.
- Add metadata-only active gateway request snapshots and idle/deadline diagnostics. Preserve current upstream streaming, model-turn admission, compaction classification and cancellation behavior.
- Surface malformed tool-argument failures with request identifiers, retain private argument diagnostics, and keep child timeout failures in child records instead of the lead assistant's message stream.

Merge order: **merge PR #184 first, then this PR after its checks pass**. This branch includes PR #184 head `a3dece01` and current `feat/jiuwenswarm`; after #184 merges, its benchmark files drop out of this PR's diff. PR #146 is no longer a prerequisite. PR #190's bounded output-limit recovery is separate and is not required by this PR.

Validation on the refreshed branch:
- 169 focused API/workspace tests passed.
- 14 biomedical gateway tests passed, including arXiv TLS and redacted HTTP diagnostics.
- Full workspace build and typecheck passed; 21 CI self-tests passed.
- Five targeted mocked Swarm E2E cases passed (LR-05/06 in both dispatch orders, plus LR-07 disconnect recovery), without skips or relaxed assertions. Remote CI is running on refreshed head `e74da43b`.
- Earlier live validation reproduced the original 406 and returned HTTP 200 for two recorded DRB-62 queries (15 and 10 records) and a fresh MCP query (five records). These live requests were not repeated during this branch refresh.

Limits: the observed 406 workaround is not a general fix for arXiv 429 or local queue timeouts. Logging is diagnostic, not rate-limit recovery. This PR does not claim to recover output-token exhaustion automatically; that behavior is developed in #190. Real research experiments using the skill/arXiv changes do not establish that all benchmark or quality checks pass.

recent_merged.title: fix(research): recover arXiv searches and improve literature E2E

recent_merged.author: zy95-12
recent_merged.body:
When a model exhausts its output budget, truncated tool arguments currently become a gateway failure, and reasoning-only responses end the task without an answer. Partial text can also be mistaken for a completed answer. This change keeps the task running for up to two recovery attempts, while preventing tools from the truncated response from executing.

The gateway withholds tool arguments until the response completes, preserves `finish_reason=length` and usage, and emits SSE comments while arguments are buffered. A per-instance Swarm model wrapper rejects truncated responses before argument repair or tool execution and asks the model to perform one small action or write a smaller batch. Recovery uses the existing model, context, turn admission, cancellation and deadlines; it does not replay completed operations or increase token limits. Exhaustion fails with diagnostics and preserves existing artifacts. Ordinary provider and transport failures remain separate.

Validation:
- 106 related API tests passed.
- 60 pinned Swarm boundary tests passed, including a real ReAct loop driven by controlled model responses: the truncated call never executes, the recovered call executes once, and the run completes.
- Full workspace typecheck and architecture checks passed.
- DRB-59 and TC-E2E-01 are running concurrently in an isolated experiment with memory graph disabled; real E2E outcomes are pending. DRB-59 uses RACE scoring; TC-E2E-01 retains its internal evaluator and contract checks.

This PR targets `feat/jiuwenswarm` independently. PR 171 skill/arXiv changes and real-experiment configuration are combined only in the separate experiment branch, not included here. ## Summary

This PR retains the late-enabled ScienceMemory goal backfill and adds fixes for issues found during manual browser exploration of the JiuwenSwarm workflows:

- Keep the Skill Library summary proposal count global while the selected-library list remains scoped.
- Treat numeric data arrays as data, not literature citations, during offline Reviewer precheck.
- Hand a uniquely named nested workspace file to a subagent when the prompt mentions only its basename; ambiguous names remain excluded.
- Allow a parent task MCP call to outlast its child execution window.
- Guide the agent to fall back to read_skill when native skill_tool hits a filesystem lock, without attempting host-path access from the sandbox.

The branch includes the latest feat/jiuwenswarm base, including the upstream dedicated MCP transport patch. No temporary global SDK monkey patch is included.

## Validation status

- Source checks on the merged branch: pnpm build and pnpm typecheck passed; git diff --check passed before commit.
- Earlier focused memory validation on the original memory commit: API unit tests 101 passed; the late-goal regression passed against the local backend. The prior browser run with real Kimi observed the goal and linked-subtask counts increase after enabling ScienceMemory late.
- Earlier exploratory browser runs exposed the additional issues above. The old Docker image confirmed that a 305-second child command completed but the parent lost its result at the 300-second boundary.
- The newly pushed commit d1e3b7cc has not yet been manually retested in a rebuilt Docker image. That browser verification is the next step.
- GitHub Actions run 36020332737 (head 30e071a0) confirms the reviewed local-backend late-goal regression appears in the frozen PR UT plan and its per-case execution result is PASS. UT totals: 3,607 planned, 3,607 executed, 3,607 passed, 0 skipped. The Neo4j variant remains status:external.
- Local UT/ST/E2E suites were not run for this update, per operator request. GitHub Actions run 36020332737 completed successfully: UT, ST, mocked E2E, Docker image, both binary jobs, and Coverage all passed.

## Release

recent_merged.author: zy95-12
recent_merged.body:
When native `task` dispatch runs multiple Swarm children, every child's authority snapshot currently embeds the session-wide subagent catalog. Growing one sibling's tool transcript therefore inflates the other children's checkpoints. The child collector also receives the parent run ID, selecting the parent's execution provenance instead of its own.

This change gives snapshot collection an explicit session/execution/task scope. Children capture their own task, execution provenance, inbox, timers, shell executions and transfers. The native parent retains the task directory. Directory entries reference immutable `SubagentAuthority` records containing the complete task record and continuation-context reference; unchanged catalog objects reuse their reference. UI/task APIs retain their full records, and shared artifact versions, permissions and environment authorities remain captured. Historical records and closure integrity checks are preserved without a catalog migration.

In the regression fixture, adding 2.4 MB of sibling tool output leaves the other child's authority snapshot identical. The parent's two-entry task directory is 569 bytes, while both the old and new full task records remain readable by immutable reference.

Validation:
- API dependency build and API typecheck passed.
- 36 focused authority, notification, shell, transfer, continuation and native-versioning tests passed.
- 97 Swarm adapter, AgentRun and subagent-lifecycle tests passed.
- All 5 new tests executed under the PR profile: 5 passed, 0 skipped. They cover sibling-growth isolation, owner provenance/inbox, immutable revisions and cold reload, missing-reference rejection, cross-session rejection, and shell/transfer ownership.
- Architecture checks passed (53 script tests plus boundary validation); Markdown lint passed.

Based directly on upstream `feat/jiuwenswarm` at `60626de2`, which already includes #182. This does not depend on #146, #171, #183 or #184.

Scope: this is the state-isolation change. It does not optimize repeated historical closure traversal or every shared-resource snapshot, change timeout limits, or establish that DRB-59/DRB-75 now finish successfully. Real E2E benchmarks have not been rerun for this branch. English and Chinese architecture notes document these boundaries.
recent_merged.head: fix/agent-snapshot-scope
recent_merged.title: fix(agent): isolate native task authority snapshots across Swarm children

recent_merged.author: zy95-12
recent_merged.body:
Add configurable FIFO task admission (1–10 children), hard wall-clock deadlines, cancellation and child-owned workspace handoff. The platform task bridge remains the default for Swarm UT, with an explicit native-delegation override.

A parent and child with different skill counts previously generated different shared MCP schemas even after their literal values were removed. This unnecessarily re-registered every tool and permission before the child reached its model, sometimes exhausting a 10-second task budget. Normalize equivalent union schemas, preserve the original model-facing constraints, and remove persisted permissions only when their MCP generation has no active users. Add metadata-only initialization timings and regression tests for generation reuse and permission isolation.

Split from #146, which remains unchanged. Merge this PR before #183 and #184; all remain Draft and target `feat/jiuwenswarm`. The branch includes the latest merged prerequisites through `7ad18de5`.

Validation: full build; 64 task/workspace/settings tests; 225 hermetic adapter tests; all 72 API tests selected by the CI plan pass locally through real Swarm, with coverage and two CPU cores. The child's registration phase dropped from approximately 6.2 seconds to less than 1 ms in the reproduced case. The original 10-second deadline and model-entry assertions remain unchanged. Latest GitHub CI is still running.

closed_recent.body:
> Related: #27 (the README itself reads well after the rework, so this issue is about what the reader meets next), #117 (the tutorials the indexes should list), #118 (the capability entries the indexes should list).

## Summary

After the README, a new reader lands on a language index. PR 122 already reorders the indexes into a sensible first-use sequence, but the how-to list now opens with connector configuration and the Getting started section does not say what each page assumes. The buckets below the index also have no landing pages and their names are not defined in the repository, and the standard-pages issue delivers those. I would like this issue to finish the ordering around the first-use path, without renaming anything.

## Current state

Verified against PR #122 head f1e18c5:

- `docs/en/README.md` and `docs/zh/README.md` already order their sections as Getting started, Core capabilities, Domain guides, How-to guides, Reference, Developer documentation. This satisfies the section-ordering part of the original ask.
- The how-to list now starts with "Configure custom MCP servers". Deployment moved to `getting-started/deployment.md` and the literature case moved to `domains/literature-research.md`, so the five remaining how-to pages are connector configuration, JiuwenSwarm, network proxy, an evolution search, and ScienceMemory setup. A reader who just finished the quick start meets connector configuration first.
- Five buckets have no landing page in either language: `getting-started`, `core`, `domains`, `how-to` and `reference`. Only `developer-docs` has a README (`docs/en/developer-docs/README.md`, `docs/zh/developer-docs/README.md`). A reader who jumps to a bucket lands on a bare file list.
- What each bucket is for is written only in the PR 122 description. `docs/README.md` names the six buckets in one sentence and defines none of them. Names like `core` and `domains` are not self-explanatory.

## What to write

1. Order or group the how-to list by when a new user needs it. The current list opens with connector configuration and the rest are configuration or advanced features. Consider short labels such as "Connect and configure" and "Run and operate", or a sentence that points deployment and the literature case to `getting-started` and `domains`.
2. Make the Getting started section of both indexes state what each page assumes, now that the tutorial mode was dropped and its role sits in getting-started and domains.

The five section landing pages and the written bucket definitions are owned by the standard-pages issue, tracked separately, so the two issues do not double-own them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both language indexes order or group their entries so a new reader can pick the next document without knowing internal terms.
- [ ] The Getting started section of both indexes states what each page assumes.
- [ ] The six bucket names (getting-started, core, domains, how-to, reference, developer-docs) stay as shipped by PR 122, and the language-index order stays Getting started, Core capabilities, Domain guides, How-to guides, Reference, Developer documentation. This issue does not rename or move buckets.

## Open questions

- Should the how-to index be grouped under short subheadings, or stay a flat list in priority order?
- The tutorial mode was dropped in PR 122. Should getting-started and domains formally absorb the tutorial role, or should a separate tutorials bucket return?
- Do the names `core` and `domains` hold, given that neither is a Diátaxis mode and `core` is nearly empty?

## Out of scope

- Writing the tutorial or capability content (owned by #117 and #118).
- Delivering the five section landing pages and the written bucket definitions (owned by the standard-pages issue, tracked separately).
- The quick start's Next steps links (owned by the tutorial batch).
- Renaming the six buckets or moving pages between them.
- The public site repository. It will sync the product docs on a nightly job, so its navigation update is deferred and out of scope here.

Docs baseline: `feat/jiuwenswarm` @ 9670568.

### 📚 Documentation Issue Description

> Related: #116 (first-run installation troubleshooting), #118 (capability entries), #119 (entry-point order). The landing pages and the bucket definitions overlap with #119's navigation ask, so this issue owns their delivery and #119 owns the ordering.

## Summary

PR 122 reorganizes the docs into six buckets per language, but the scaffolding that makes a bucket usable is missing. Five of the six buckets have no landing page, the meaning of each bucket is written only in the PR description, and the user tree has no security page, no general FAQ and no glossary. I would like these standard pages added on top of the structure PR 122 ships.

## Current state

Verified against 0e904661:

- Twelve content directories (six buckets, two languages), and only `developer-docs` has a README in each language. `getting-started`, `core`, `domains`, `how-to` and `reference` have none, so a reader who jumps to a bucket lands on a bare file list.
- What each bucket is for exists only in the PR 122 description. `docs/README.md` names the six buckets in one sentence and defines none of them. Names like `core` and `domains` are not self-explanatory.
- No security or trust page exists in the user tree. The only security text is the multi-user WARNING in `README.md:85-86` (and `README_zh.md:85-86`), which covers loopback binding, the single bearer token, the absence of TLS and the sandbox boundary. The one page that explains isolation, `sandbox-execution.md`, sits in `docs/en/developer-docs/` and `docs/zh/developer-docs/`.
- No general troubleshooting or FAQ page exists. Troubleshooting exists only as per-task sections: the Docker section inside `docs/en/getting-started/deployment.md`, short `## Troubleshooting` sections in `docs/en/how-to/configure-custom-mcp.md:91` and `docs/en/how-to/run-with-jiuwenswarm.md:103`, and a `## 5. Troubleshooting` section in `docs/en/how-to/science-memory-setup.md:187`. The first-run, installation-recovery path is already asked for in #116, which is narrower than a general FAQ.
- No glossary exists. Terms such as Project and Session (used in `docs/en/getting-started/quick-start.md:48`), and Skill, Specialist, Connector, Reviewer and workspace (used across `docs/en/reference/runtime-behavior.md`), have no single definition a new reader can look up.

## What to write

1. Section landing pages. Add a `README.md` to each of the five index-less buckets in both languages, using one template: what this bucket is for, when a reader should come here, and one line for each child page.
2. Bucket definitions. Write the six definitions into `docs/README.md`, so the classification rule lives in the repository and not only in the pull request.
3. Security and trust page. Add a user-facing page in both languages that states the loopback and single-token defaults, the absence of TLS, the fail-closed sandbox and what runs outside it, and the "not a multi-user service" boundary. Link `docs/en/developer-docs/sandbox-execution.md` for depth instead of repeating it.
4. General troubleshooting and FAQ. Add a page in both languages covering model connection failures, permission cards, connector and proxy failures, run timeouts, and where data lives. Keep first-run installation recovery in #116 and link to it.
5. Glossary. Add a page in both languages defining at least Project, Session, Skill, Specialist, Connector, Reviewer and workspace, and link it from the language index.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of `getting-started`, `core`, `domains`, `how-to` and `reference` has a landing page in both languages, following one template.
- [ ] `docs/README.md` defines what each of the six buckets is for.
- [ ] A security and trust page exists in both user trees and links the sandbox design page.
- [ ] A general troubleshooting or FAQ page exists in both languages and is distinct from the first-run recovery in #116.
- [ ] A glossary page defines at least Project, Session, Skill, Specialist, Connector, Reviewer and workspace.
- [ ] Each new page is linked from its language index, and each landing page links its child pages.

## Open questions

- Should the bucket definitions live in `docs/README.md`, in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, or on a dedicated documentation-style page?
- Does the security page need maintainer sign-off on what is safe to claim before it is published?
- Should the glossary be one page per language, or a section of the documentation home?

## Out of scope

- Page frontmatter and a page status or version schema.
- A machine-readable `llms.txt` or `llms-full.txt` export.
- Changelog or release-notes pages.
- Contributor guides for adding a tool, skill, connector or provider.
- These lower-priority page types are recorded in the audit's deferred list and are not tracked here.

> Complements the still-open #46 (its release-link, verification, ordering, and naming
> asks are tracked there). Related: #1, #27, #29, #35, #38.

## Summary

The rewritten READMEs now answer two of the onboarding questions at the README level. They
name release 0.2.0 and the arm64 asset, so a reader can obtain the binary, and the
Requirements table maps the binary, source, and Docker paths to host requirements. What
remains sits in the deployment guide and in one link convention. The three-mode comparison
still has no operating-system column, so the OS facts are scattered across the local-mode,
Docker, and artifact-name lines. The binary section still opens by building from source,
with no walkthrough from a published release asset to `serve`. Binary and local modes have
no first-run troubleshooting block, while Docker does. And the README download command
pins a version and a filename, so the command goes stale at the next release. Neither
README states that the prebuilt binary is the shortest path and that the other modes are
in the deployment guide, and the deployment guide never states what it is for.
I would like those things fixed, in both languages.

## Current state

- `README.md` and `README_zh.md` are both 103 lines. The installation section (README line
  24, paragraph to line 36) names release 0.2.0 (line 26), gives a fixed-version download
  command (lines 29-31), distinguishes the local service token from a model API key (line
  34), and mentions the arm64 asset, Bubblewrap as the only host dependency, and the
  deployment guide for source and Docker (line 36). The Requirements section (line 71,
  table lines 73-77, columns Path and Host requirements) already maps the three paths to
  operating systems.
- The deployment guide is 443 lines in English and 451 in Chinese. It opens with a
  three-mode comparison (EN lines 5-15, header line 7). The table columns are Mode, What
  the user receives, Host dependencies, and Intended use. No column states supported
  operating systems.
- Operating-system support is scattered. The binary artifact names appear at lines 24-25,
  local mode states Linux x86_64/aarch64 and macOS x64/arm64 at line 147, and the Docker
  prerequisites state Linux x86_64 or aarch64 at line 189.
- The binary section opens with `### Build and run` (line 19) and teaches building the
  artifact from source. Nothing walks a reader from a published release asset to `serve`.
- The local service token versus a model API key is explained in the README (line 34) and
  the quick start (`docs/en/getting-started/quick-start.md`, line 44). Token rejection
  recovery appears in the quick start (line 30) and in the Docker FAQ (deployment guide line 406),
  but the installation section does not link a recovery passage directly. #35 shows the
  confusion is real.
- The guide's only FAQ-style troubleshooting sits inside the Docker section (EN
  `### Frequently asked questions`, line 394, running to the `### Limitations` heading at
  line 426). It covers build failures, data-directory permissions, port conflicts, token
  rejection (line 406), degraded health, and sandbox failures. Binary mode documents
  Bubblewrap (lines 64-77) and local mode carries a Seatbelt note (lines 150 and 177), but
  neither mode has an FAQ covering token rejection, degraded health, or port conflicts.
  The quick start explains a `degraded` status at line 38 without linking a recovery
  passage.
- Neither README frames the prebuilt binary as the shortest path; line 36 only notes that
  source and Docker are covered in the deployment guide. The deployment guide opens by
  pointing back at the README's shortest path (line 3), but never states what the guide
  itself is for, so a reader has to infer why they would open it.
- #1 asked how to obtain the binary. The rewritten README now names release 0.2.0 and the
  fixed-version download command, so that question is answered at the README level. #46
  asked for release links, SHA-256 verification instructions, a deployment guide led by
  downloading rather than building, and aligned configuration entry names. The decision
  and recovery layers above are still open.

## What to write

1. Add a supported-operating-systems column to the three-mode comparison in both
   deployment guides (binary: Linux x86_64/aarch64, source: Linux and macOS, Docker:
   Linux).
2. Lead the binary section with downloading a published release asset, then give the
   build-from-source procedure.
3. Add a first-run troubleshooting block for binary and local modes (Docker already has
   one), covering at least token rejection and where the Connection settings live, a
   `degraded` health status, a missing `bwrap`, and where the logs are. Link it from the
   README or the quick start.
4. Change the README download command (lines 29-31) to point at the generic Releases page,
   or use clearly labeled version and architecture placeholders and explain how to choose
   the asset from the Release page.
5. State in both READMEs that the prebuilt binary is the shortest path and that the other
   modes (a source-built single-file binary, local source mode, Docker) are covered in the
   deployment guide.
6. State at the top of both deployment guides what the guide is for: the other ways to
   install and run ScienceDiscovery, for portable artifacts, container operations, and
   development.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The mode comparison in both deployment guides states the supported operating systems
  per mode.
- [ ] The binary section leads with downloading a published release asset before the
  build-from-source procedure, in both languages.
- [ ] The binary and local modes have a first-run troubleshooting block in both languages,
  linked from the README or the quick start, covering token rejection and where the
  Connection settings live, `degraded` health, a missing `bwrap`, and log location.
- [ ] The README download command points at the generic Releases page, or uses clearly
  labeled placeholders and explains asset selection.
- [ ] Both READMEs name the prebuilt binary as the shortest path and point the other modes
  at the deployment guide.
- [ ] Both deployment guides state their role at the top.
- [ ] The English and Chinese paths describe the same confirmed behavior and platform
  matrix.

## Open questions

- Is Docker positioned as an equal path for new users, or as an advanced option? This
  decides how prominent it is in the mode comparison.
- The packaging output includes `SHA256SUMS`. Confirm whether the published release assets
  carry it, and if so, add the verification step #46 asked for.
- Do update and uninstall instructions belong in the deployment guide now, or in a later
  pass?
- Should this issue absorb #46's remaining verification and ordering asks, or leave them
  with #46? Maintainers' call.

## Out of scope

- Changing the release process or adding build artifacts.
- Documenting unsupported platforms.
- The product fixes tracked in #29, #35, and #38. This issue only links their recovery
  documentation.
- Reordering the documentation indexes (tracked separately).

closed_recent.body:
## Problem

The `CI` workflow executes the Node and Python unit tests twice.

1. The `UT` job runs `pnpm ci:ut`. That is the gate: with the tagged test plan from #126 it runs the UT slice of the shared plan, selected from source tags and a fixed profile, with every Node test file in a worker of its own and the Python suites through the plan's pytest adapter. The job fails unless every planned case executes and passes. It records no coverage.
2. The `Coverage` job then checks the repository out again and runs `pnpm coverage:node` and `node scripts/run-python-coverage.mjs`, which execute the unit tests a second time under instrumentation. With the plan from #126 they select the very same cases the gate just ran. On a pull request the second run covers only the directories the diff touched; on the nightly schedule it repeats the whole suite.

The second run costs a full test execution per pipeline, and it is a second execution path. The numbers it reports describe a run that is not the one that gated the change. Whenever the two paths differ in how they execute a test — process isolation, interpreter setup, which cases a directory contains — the coverage run passes or fails on its own terms, independently of the gate. Two concrete ways this goes wrong:

- Running a Python service's whole test directory executes cases the gate's profile deliberately leaves out, such as the `status:external` cases in `services/memory-graph` that need a live Neo4j. On a runner without Neo4j those fail the Coverage job while the gate is green.
- Running a directory's Node test files in one shared process lets files interfere with each other's globals. The gate runs each file in its own worker, so cases that pass in the gate can fail under coverage.

## Expected behaviour

- The job that runs the plan records coverage while it runs it. Node workers run with `--experimental-test-coverage` in the same per-file isolation the gate already uses; the Python suites run with `coverage run` in front of the same pytest invocation.
- That job uploads the coverage data as an artifact.
- The `Coverage` job depends on it, downloads the artifact, merges the data and writes the summary. It executes no test. If the producing job failed, the summary is built from whatever was uploaded and states that the job failed; nothing is re-run to fill the gap.
- Pull requests and the nightly run report on exactly the plan the gate ran. There is no separate diff-based selection of what to measure.
- ST and the mocked browser E2E do not load product modules into a measured process, so they contribute no module coverage. The summary says so instead of reporting numbers for them.
- Test selection does not change: source tags and a fixed profile, never the runner's services, credentials or host.

## Acceptance

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has no step in the `Coverage` job that runs a test command.
- The coverage files the `Coverage` job reports on come from the gate job's own run.
- A local run of the UT layer produces the same coverage files, and the reporting command runs on them without executing any test.

### 🚀 Background Description


The coverage job currently generates and uploads Node.js and Python JSON summary artifacts, but the Actions run page does not expose the results directly. Contributors must download artifacts to see what was scanned and the aggregate coverage, unlike E2E results that are visible in the run summary.

This feature should make coverage results visible without introducing a minimum percentage gate.

### Design Ideas

Write a repository-owned Markdown renderer to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` from the existing `coverage/summary.json` and `coverage/python/summary.json`.

Acceptance criteria:
- Show Node.js and Python separately.
- Label full, incremental, skipped, failed, or unavailable scans.
- Show measured files/groups and available line, branch, and function totals.
- List selected groups for incremental scans.
- Keep coverage informational: no minimum percentage.
- Preserve current failure semantics and artifact uploads.

### Involved Public APIs

None. This changes only GitHub Actions reporting and repository-owned CI scripts.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

The change touches `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the existing Node.js/Python coverage scripts and selector rules, and the operational CI contract in `.ci/README.md`. Runtime APIs and product behavior are unaffected.

### Test Design and Test Plan

- Unit-test the summary renderer for full, incremental, skipped, failed, and unavailable results.
- Test that changes to the renderer select full Node.js and Python coverage.
- Parse the workflow YAML after editing.
- Run the WSL build, recursive workspace tests, and architecture checks.
- Confirm coverage remains informational and coverage test failures still fail the job.

### Additional Information

An implementation is prepared on `wyhohyw:codex/coverage-actions-summary`; a Draft PR will link this issue.

closed_recent.body:
### 🚀 Background Description


ScienceDiscovery contains maintained Python services whose tests are not represented by the Node.js coverage percentage. A Node-only number must not be presented as whole-repository coverage.

This issue adds a separate Python coverage pipeline using mature Python tooling. It complements the Node.js coverage issue #137 while keeping the two languages' commands, reports, and scope independently auditable.

### Design Ideas

### Measurement

- Use `coverage.py` as the coverage engine; do not implement a custom Python tracer.
- Preserve existing test frameworks:
  - `services/gateway` and `services/paper`: `unittest`
  - `services/memory-graph` and `services/evolve`: `pytest`
- Run each existing suite under `coverage run --branch --parallel-mode`, then use `coverage combine`.
- Measure production source directories, not test files.
- Record covered/total counts and percentages for lines and branches. Keep service/path groups separate.

### CI execution

- Reuse existing CI and nightly workflows rather than adding a standalone coverage workflow.
- PR/default-branch runs should select affected Python services where the dependency/selector mapping is reliable. A partial run must be explicitly marked partial and must never be displayed as whole-Python coverage.
- The existing nightly run should execute the complete Python coverage scope and publish the authoritative baseline.
- Coverage remains informational initially; existing test failures still fail the job.

### Reports and artifact

- Generate `coverage.py` JSON as the structured source consumed by the board.
- Optionally generate Cobertura XML for future GitHub Code Quality integration and LCOV/HTML for local diagnosis, without making a paid GitHub feature a prerequisite.
- Upload one SHA-qualified Actions artifact containing aggregate and per-service JSON summaries plus run identity metadata.
- Use repository default artifact retention.

### Dashboard

- Display Node.js and Python coverage as separate first-class metrics.
- If an overall line percentage is shown, compute it from summed covered/total lines:
  `(node covered + python covered) / (node total + python total)`.
- Never average percentages directly.
- Label nightly baselines as authoritative and partial/incremental results explicitly.

### Involved Public APIs

No product runtime or public API changes are proposed.

This feature adds an internal Python coverage artifact contract. It should align with the Node summary's run/SHA/mode/group metadata while retaining Python-specific metrics and source paths.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `services/gateway` and `services/paper` keep their existing `unittest` commands.
- `services/memory-graph` and `services/evolve` keep their existing `pytest` commands and extras.
- CI test selection and nightly scheduling determine whether the result is partial or authoritative.
- The status board consumes the structured Actions artifact; it does not run Python tests itself.
- GitHub Code Quality can consume Cobertura XML later, but this feature must work without enabling the paid service.

### Test Design and Test Plan

- Add focused coverage runs for every maintained Python service and verify existing tests still execute with the same pass/fail semantics.
- Test combining parallel coverage data from `unittest` and `pytest` environments.
- Verify branch coverage is enabled and test files are excluded from production totals.
- Verify missing/failed service runs cannot produce an authoritative aggregate.
- Verify partial PR results and complete nightly baselines have distinct metadata.
- Validate JSON totals against `coverage report` for representative services.
- Add board parser/rendering tests for Python-only, Node-only, combined, missing, and stale artifacts.
- Verify overall coverage uses summed covered/total values, not the arithmetic mean of percentages.
- Run the complete repository test suite before merging.

### Additional Information

Related work:

- Node.js coverage tracking: #137
- Node.js WIP implementation: #134
- Companion status-board PR: https://github.com/ScienceDiscovery/github-status-board/pull/1
- coverage.py documentation: https://coverage.readthedocs.io/

Non-goals: migrating all Python tests to one framework, implementing a custom coverage engine, or requiring GitHub Code Quality/another paid service.

closed_recent.body:
### 🚀 Background Description


ScienceDiscovery runs Node.js tests in CI but does not yet publish a durable, machine-readable coverage result tied to the exact workflow run and commit. Maintainers should be able to inspect coverage in GitHub Actions, while the status board should consume the same CI evidence without running tests itself or parsing unstable console text.

This issue covers **Node.js coverage only**. Python coverage should be tracked separately so that the tools, test commands, scope, and percentages remain explicit.

The current work-in-progress implementation is PR #134.

### Design Ideas

### Measurement

- Reuse the repository's existing built Node.js tests; do not introduce another test tier or migrate test frameworks.
- Run them with Node.js 22's built-in `--experimental-test-coverage` collector (V8 coverage).
- Group results by workspace/path and keep repository CI-script tests as explicit groups.
- Exclude test sources from production-source totals.
- Record covered/total counts and percentages for lines, branches, and functions rather than storing percentages alone.

### CI execution

- Integrate coverage into the existing `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; do not add a second coverage workflow.
- For pull requests and default-branch pushes, select changed Node.js workspaces and their transitive dependents. Changes to shared coverage infrastructure select every group.
- Reuse the existing nightly workflow for a complete, authoritative all-group baseline.
- Skip coverage for release-only calls.
- Test failures still fail the job. Coverage percentages are informational initially and do not introduce a new threshold gate.

### Actions artifact

- Generate LCOV only as a local intermediate.
- Upload one SHA-qualified artifact containing aggregate and per-group JSON summaries.
- Include source SHA, base SHA, generation time, mode (`incremental` or `full`), selected groups, and whether the result is authoritative.
- Use the repository's default artifact retention; do not introduce independent 30/90-day policies.

### Status-board consumption

- The board downloads the structured summary through the GitHub Actions Artifacts API. It does not execute tests and does not infer coverage from log text.
- Show the latest full nightly baseline, per-path line/branch/function coverage, nightly history, and recent PR affected-group results.
- A homepage value composed from later default-branch group summaries must be labelled as an estimate until the next full nightly run recalibrates it.

### Involved Public APIs

No product runtime or public API changes are proposed.

The feature adds an internal CI artifact contract for coverage summaries. Consumers must treat the run identity, SHA, mode, selected groups, and authoritative flag as part of that contract.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Existing CI and nightly workflows provide the execution environment.
- Existing Node workspace dependency metadata is used to expand changed workspaces to transitive dependents.
- The companion status board reads the Actions artifact and renders the coverage page.
- Browser/TSX, Python, and Playwright coverage are explicitly excluded from this issue and must not be represented as covered by the Node percentage.
- GitHub Code Quality/Cobertura upload can be evaluated separately; it is not required for the initial board integration.

### Test Design and Test Plan

- Add selector tests for changed workspaces, transitive dependents, shared-infrastructure full selection, and irrelevant-path skips.
- Add aggregation tests that exclude test sources and preserve aggregate and per-group covered/total values.
- Validate that PR/default-branch CI publishes affected-group summaries from the existing CI workflow.
- Validate that nightly publishes a complete authoritative baseline without a second workflow.
- Verify that every artifact is tied to its workflow run/SHA and contains only the structured JSON required by consumers.
- Verify that test failures still fail the coverage job.
- Add status-board tests distinguishing authoritative nightly data, incremental/PR data, estimates, and UT/ST/E2E artifacts.
- Run the repository's complete existing test suite before merging.

### Additional Information

Related work:

- WIP implementation: #134
- Companion status-board PR: https://github.com/ScienceDiscovery/github-status-board/pull/1
- Design in the implementation branch: `docs/designs/test-coverage.v3.md`

Acceptance boundary: the resulting percentage covers built Node.js workspace tests and repository CI-script tests only. It must never be presented as whole-repository coverage.
